DOC1 INTRODUCTION

General information

The information contained in this document applies only to the software versions specified on the title page.
Not all functions available in the product may be described in this documentation; in such cases, Donatoni Macchine is under no obligation to guarantee these functions or retain them in future versions.
This document is supplied as the “Section B” software appendix to the machine use and maintenance manual.

Purpose of the manual

This manual provides the operating instructions required for a thorough understanding of the Parametrix program, together with useful information for troubleshooting malfunctions.
Correct operation, service life and cost-effective use of the machine depend on compliance with the instructions in this manual.
The machine use and maintenance manual and this software manual must always be available at the installation site, kept in a safe and readily accessible place. If either manual is lost, contact the person responsible for prevention and protection services.
Failure to comply with the instructions in this manual, negligence, or improper and unsuitable use of the machine may cause the Manufacturer to void the warranty provided for the machine and may prevent the machine from delivering the benefits for which it was designed.
DONATONI MACCHINE SRL remains available to provide prompt and accurate technical assistance and any support that may help ensure optimum machine operation and maximum performance.
The Manufacturer reserves the right, at its own discretion, to modify this publication and the data contained herein whenever this is considered necessary for the technical or commercial improvement of the product.

Safekeeping of the manual

This Software Manual must be kept throughout the machine's entire operating life, including if the machine is transferred to a third party.
To ensure that the Software Manual is stored correctly, observe the following recommendations:

  • Use the Manual in a way that does not damage all or part of its contents; in particular, do not leave the Manual unattended during use and return it to its designated location immediately after consultation;

  • Do not remove, tear out or rewrite any part of the Manual for any reason;

  • Keep the Manual in an area protected from humidity, heat and other environmental agents that could compromise its integrity or service life;

  • If all or part of this Manual is lost or damaged, request a copy of the documentation from the Manufacturer.

DOC2 ON-MACHINE PROGRAMS

When the application starts, if the axes have already been homed, the following home screen is displayed:

Top bar

Parameters
Provides access to the Parametrix program parameters.

Tool Parameters
Pressing the button opens the tool parameters page. See the “Tool Configuration” chapter for a detailed description of the parameters page.

Automatic 0/90-degree rotation
The “C” axis automatically moves to 0 or 90 degrees when the button is pressed.

Automatic parking
When the button is pressed, the machine automatically moves the “X”, “Y”, “Z” and “C” axes to the zero position.
The machine performs the movements in the following order:
(A) - “Z” axis to the absolute zero position;
(B) - “C” axis to the absolute 0 position;
(C) - “X” and “Y” axes simultaneously to the absolute zero position;

WARNING!

Certain safety conditions must be met before automatic parking can be performed:
The “A” axis must be at 0_.
Make sure that the movement area involved in positioning (see adjacent figure) is clear.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the tool.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

External water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

Manual Tool Change
Pressing the button starts the tool-change procedure.

Maintenance
Pressing this button displays a window containing all machine maintenance operations.
Both maintenance operations that are due and those that are within the normal interval are displayed.

Help
Pressing this button slightly changes the appearance and behaviour of all buttons currently displayed. Any button with a small question mark in the top-left corner can then be pressed to display a short message explaining its function. To exit this help mode, simply press the “Help” button again.

Common interface elements

The graphical interface elements shared by the various functions are:

Axes

This interface displays the values of the machine axes.

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes already homed:

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes not yet homed:

The elements in this common interface section are explained below, using the already-homed axes configuration as a reference.

Actual position: indicates the position of the axis relative to the active origin.
Target position: indicates the position to be set in order to move the axis by pressing the MDI or RTCP button.
F: Feed, movement speed expressed in mm/min.
DTG: Distance To Go, distance from the target.
A: Amperes.

Reset Axis
Pressing this button sets the zero point of the active origin at the current position of the corresponding axis (X, Y or Z).
The axis reset operation can only be performed for origins other than 0 (zero).
To use the tool-coordinate origin (TCP), the correct dimensions of the mounted tool must be set before pressing the Reset Axis button.

Automatic _90-degree rotation
The position of the “C” axis is increased by 90 degrees clockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 12 degrees, pressing the “Automatic _90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 102 degrees: 12 _ 90.

Automatic -90-degree rotation
The position of the “C” axis is decreased by 90 degrees anticlockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 102 degrees, pressing the “Automatic -90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 12 degrees: 102 - 90.

Controls

This panel contains several buttons whose behaviour is explained below:

Interpolation mode
When the button is active (right-hand figure), manual Z, C and A movements are performed taking rotation and inclination into account.
Interpolated Z-axis movement: when the Z-axis JOG is operated, the machine moves in alignment with the mounted tool.

NOTE

The selected tool type affects the direction of movement.

Interpolated C-axis movement: when the C-axis control is operated, the X and Y axes move in addition to the rotation so that the inner edge of the blade (or the tip of the tool) remains stationary.
Interpolated A-axis movement: when the A-axis control is operated, the X, Y and Z axes move in addition to the inclination so that the inner edge of the blade (or the tip of the tool) remains stationary in its current position.
Simultaneous movements of the Z, C and A axes are not permitted when interpolation mode is active.

WARNING!

Pay close attention to the status of the button, as the machine movements may differ from those expected.

RTCP Interpolation
Performs positioning to the “Target” value set for the A or C axis while keeping the inner edge of the blade (or the tip of the tool) stationary.
For further details, see the paragraph: “RTCP Rotation Tool Center Point Semi-Automatic Function”.

MDI
When pressed, the machine moves until it reaches the values set as the target positions (see above).
The speed of the X and Y axes is controlled by their respective potentiometers, while the other axes are controlled by the interpolated potentiometer.

Tool

This interface element displays the main information about the tool mounted on the machine.

Example of a tool mounted on the machine: Saw blade

Example of a tool mounted on the machine: Core drill

Active tool
Clicking this button displays a confirmation pop-up that allows the operator to change the type of tool mounted on the machine.

The available choices are limited to:

  1. Disk

  2. Milling cutter / Core drill

Origin

Clicking the “Origin” field displays a small on-screen numeric keypad that allows the operator to select a different origin for machining.
Origin values can range from 0 to 19 inclusive.

Example with origin 0:

Example with origin 10:

Advanced origin settings

Pressing the options button above the origin opens a panel providing a centralised view of all available origins and their associated values. The active origin can be changed by clicking the corresponding row.

RTCP - Rotation Tool Center Point

The RTCP function allows the operator to position the machine for a miter cut while keeping the tool height unchanged, even though the inclination changes during positioning. The inner edge of the saw blade remains in the same position as at the start of the movement.

Operating procedure

  • Set the target position in the area dedicated to the “A” (inclination) or “C” axis.

  • Pressing the RTCP button starts the inclination or rotation function while keeping the lowest point of the tool stationary.

NOTE

Movement using the RTCP control is permitted only when the coded key is inserted in the appropriate station on the operator console.

  • Wait for the machine to reach the set position.

Motor

This section displays several statistics relating to the machine motor:

Revolutions per minute (RPM)
Indicates the spindle motor speed in revolutions per minute. The value is positive for clockwise rotation and negative for anticlockwise rotation.

Current consumption (A)
Indicates the current drawn by the spindle motor.

Alarm threshold (A)
Indicates the threshold above which the alarm is activated and spindle rotation is stopped.

Feed

The Feed value represents the machine's interpolated movement.

Right-hand sidebar

When the application starts, MANUAL is the preselected function.
This sidebar contains the following available controls and programs/functions:

Bottom bar

The bottom bar displays information and error messages, together with buttons for certain functions.
Three examples of the bottom bar are shown below:

  • No active alarms.

  • With a general emergency enabled, indicated by an icon, an error code (PE0000 in this example), its description and the flashing alarms button on the right.

  • With a displayed message; in this example, direct JOG is active.

Alarms
Allows the operator to open the alarms window.

Minimise software
Allows the operator to leave the software page.

Machine shutdown
Allows the operator to shut down the machine completely.

Alarms

The alarms page shows the system's active Alarms/Messages.
If the machine has no active alarms, the page is empty; otherwise, one row is displayed for each active error.
The following example alarm management and display page shows an alarm that is active in the system:

Alarm buttons

Refresh
Updates the status of the machine alarms.

Alarm history
Displays the daily alarm history.

Messages / Alarms
Selects whether alarms or messages are displayed.

Alarm groups
Displays complete information about the alarms currently present on the machine.

Alarm display - Standard

The standard display for an alarm consists of:

Online link
A button containing a link to the relevant online guide.

Alarm code
Identification code for the problem that caused the alarm.

Description
A brief description of the detected error.

Alarm display - History

In addition to the elements already described, the daily alarm history includes the following data:

Status change time
Date and time at which the alarm status changed.

Alarm status
Status reached by the alarm (ON / OFF).

Alarm display - Groups

The grouping system displays a single entry for each alarm, avoiding duplicates.

Number of occurrences
The number of times the alarm has been activated.

First activation time
Date and time of the first alarm activation.

Last activation time
Date and time of the most recent alarm activation.

DOC2.1 MANUAL (SUCTION CUPS)

The suction cups can be operated manually to move pieces from one work area to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable/disable suction cups
The screen shows a top view of the suction cup assembly divided into its different zones. Pressing a zone changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is configured to generate a vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is configured for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Park suction cups
Pressing the button retracts the suction cups to their rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
Pressing the button lowers the suction cups from the parking position to the limit stop. Make sure there is enough space for the suction cups to extend fully.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
Pressing the button lowers the Z axis until the material contacts the work surface, switches off the vacuum pump and activates blowing from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
This control brings the suction cups into contact with the material, activates the vacuum pump in the areas marked green and blowing in the areas marked red. When the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blowing control
The button switches blowing on or off from the suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, making sure that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that the material has no defects or breaks that could create hazards or cause machine malfunctions.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom button has no effect on the vacuum pump, which continues to operate. The pump can be forced off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, a dedicated sensor checks the vacuum status. If an adequate vacuum level is not detected, the “vacuum failure” alarm appears. The pump remains active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes the vacuum to drop rapidly, resulting in the material lifted by the suction cups falling.

DOC2.2 SINGLE CUT

In recent versions of Parametrix, the “Single Cut” function is available. Selecting “Single Cut” from the list opens a page similar to the one shown here.

Single Cut can be used to perform a straight cut (including a miter cut) on the slab, starting from the current machine position and ending at the length requested by the user. It cannot be used to cut arcs or circles.

Buttons

Parallel-cut buttons
Allows parallel movement of the machine.

Max
When the operator presses this button, the effective cutting length is determined by the current machine position and the end of the slab (the end of the slab is calculated in relation to the machine's current direction).
This value may differ from the value entered by the user in the text box.

Stop
Used after the machine has started cutting when the operator decides to reduce the cutting length. Pressing this button stops the machine and enters the length of the path cut so far in the “Length” text box.
Alternatively, the dedicated button on the console can be pressed to obtain the same behaviour as the STOP button.

Change Pass Mode
Switches between “full-depth pass” and “step pass” modes.

Save
Pressing this button saves all parameters to a file so that they can be retrieved later.

Open
Pressing this button displays a window containing all jobs previously saved by the user.
The jobs can be managed by loading their values, deleting them, or cancelling the operation and closing the panel.

Parameters

The parameters can be set differently according to the type of material to be machined and saved for subsequent similar jobs.

 

Common parameters

Single-cut length
The required cutting length must be entered in order to perform the machining operation. If the value exceeds the length that can actually be cut, the machine stops earlier.

Movement distance
Indicates the distance between one cut and the next. Only positive values can be entered in this field. For surface levelling, it is recommended to set a “movement distance” of approximately 80% of the tool thickness.

Step-pass machining configuration parameters

Penetration into the material when moving forwards
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when the machine cuts in the direction of saw-blade rotation.

Penetration into the material when moving backwards
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when cutting in the direction opposite to the tool direction.

Penetration into the material for the final pass
Indicates the cutting depth of the final tool pass through the material. This cut is always performed in the direction opposite to saw-blade movement.

Machining speed when moving forwards
Indicates the required speed for the forward cutting phase.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Machining speed when moving backwards
Indicates the required speed for the return cutting phase.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Material entry speed
Determines the speed during tool penetration into the material.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Final-pass machining speed
Indicates the speed that the machine must maintain during the final cutting pass.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

 

Full-depth-pass machining configuration parameters

Material entry speed
Determines the speed during tool penetration into the material.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Machining speed when moving forwards
Indicates the required speed for the forward cutting phase.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Executing the machining operation

To start machining, first position the machine at the required starting point. Once it is correctly positioned, enter the cutting-length value in the relevant field.

The saw blade can then be switched on using the controls on the monitor control panel. When everything is ready, start the process by pressing the “Cycle Start” button.

Machining starts in the direction in which the machine is oriented when the cut is activated; therefore, check the orientation before starting the cycle.

DOC2.3 ISO PROGRAM

The ISO file programming page is used to manage and start machining operations through .pgm files previously created using CAD-CAM programs.

List

The ISO program list, which is initially empty, contains all ISO programs that can be run sequentially.

Buttons

Open File

Add Pause

Remove selected element
Deletes a file from the list of files to be run.

Clear list

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upwards in the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down
Moves the selected ISO file downwards in the list of files to be executed.

The lower section also contains the two buttons for selecting program execution modes:

Manual / automatic
Defines whether the machine status is manual or automatic.

Single / automatic next
Defines whether the next program starts automatically.

Open file

Pressing this button displays an “Open File” window, as shown in the following image:

This window is divided into the following components:

  • File List

    • Includes all .pgm files in the currently selected directory

  • Buttons between the File List and Selected Files list

  • Selected Files List

    • Initially empty list

  • Selected File preview

    • Shows a preview of a .pgm file selected from Files or Selected Files

  • Bottom bar and search filter

Central buttons located between the “FILES” list and the “SELECTED FILES” list

Select element
Moves the selected element from the FILES list to the SELECTED FILES list.

Remove element

Insert pause

Move selected element up

The contents of the bottom bar are shown below:

Clear search filter

Sort by last modified

Alphabetical sorting

Show USB drive files

Show ISO folder

Remove file

ISO Program Code

The code of the ISO program being run is displayed in this window:

Buttons

This ISO program section contains the following buttons and functions.

Timer and Reset
Indicates the execution time of the entire .pgm file.
Pressing the button resets the timer.

ISO Preview
Enables or disables the ISO preview display.

Block search
This button is displayed only after at least one program has been loaded into the list and is used to search for a block by line.

Search for block by line
This button replaces the “Block search” button after the latter is pressed.
It allows the operator to search for a specific line of code in a small window displayed on screen.

After entering a number in the “Line number” field and pressing the “Go to” button, the ISO program code display moves to the required line, or to the last available line if the entered number exceeds the number of lines in the selected ISO program.

A block search can be ended and the “Block search” button restored by pressing the Close button:

Dry Run function (Enabled / disabled)
When this operating mode is selected, machining can be performed at the machine's maximum speed.

WARNING!

When using this function, NO material of any kind may be present during machining because the speeds specified in the ISO program are not observed during execution; the numerical control executes the entire program at the maximum rated speed achievable with interpolated axes.

ISO Test function (Enabled / disabled)
This option can be used to test the loaded file for syntax errors.
Press the “CYCLE START” button and the machine virtually processes all lines of code without moving the axes.

Suction-cup panel
Opens the suction-cup management panel.

Save
Pressing the button displays a keyboard that can be used to edit the loaded .pgm file before execution.

Block search

When running .pgm files, the block-search function can be useful for repositioning the tool at the point where the machine stopped program execution, for example if the tool jammed in the material or another stoppage occurred.

After pressing the button, the line from which machining is to continue/start can be found by entering the line number and pressing the “Search for block by line” button, or by scrolling through the file using the scroll bar beside it and selecting the required line.
After selecting the program point from which the machine is to resume the interrupted work, press the “Cycle Start” button. The machine recalculates all lines of code in the .pgm file without performing any movement. The speed of this operation depends on the number of lines of code that must be generated without movement.

Once recalculation is complete, the machine activates an automatic pause and requires the “Cycle Start” button to be pressed again to start machining.
Before starting the cycle, it is advisable to consider the machine's initial positioning, which involves all axes simultaneously.
This is necessary because the machine moves from its current position to the point where machining starts by taking the shortest route; all axes therefore move to reach that exact point.


This means, for example, that the Z axis does not lower only after reaching the starting point, but lowers gradually along the route. This could damage the machine or material if it collides with material along the path.
Depending on the current situation, the movement of one or more axes can therefore be deselected to prevent damage.
To do this, select the buttons above each axis; they change from green to red.

The buttons automatically return to green after “Cycle Start” is pressed.

View ISO

If ISO preview is enabled, an additional panel similar to the one shown below is displayed to the right of the “ISO Program Code” panel:

The ISO preview provides the following buttons:

Perspective view
Displays a 3D representation of the image.

View orthogonal to the XY plane
Displays the piece relative to the XY plane.

View orthogonal to the ZX plane
Displays the piece relative to the ZX plane.

View orthogonal to the ZY plane
Displays the piece relative to the ZY plane.

Enable or disable preview display
Enables/disables the preview display.

Executing the machining operation

The operator can create a list of PGM files by opening the required files using the dedicated load function.

Before starting execution, the order of the files in the list can optionally be changed and pauses can be inserted between executions. These pauses make the process more flexible and allow it to be stopped safely when necessary.

When the execution mode is set to "Automatic", the "ISO Test" function is also available. This is useful for checking the selected ISO program before actual execution.

To start the execution cycle, the operator must press the “Cycle Start” button. The first ISO program loaded and displayed in the list is then executed.

ISO programs can be executed in two operating modes:

In “Single” mode, program execution stops after each ISO file has been completed. Press the “Cycle Start” button again to execute the next file in the list.

“Next automatic” mode executes the ISO files in sequence without manual intervention until the end of the list.

In both modes, any pauses inserted between files allow the operator to stop the cycle at any time, ensuring continuous control over execution.

DOC2.4 SURFACE LEVELLING

The surface-levelling cycle can be used to level the worktable or the material. This program is useful when the worktable has become uneven due to cutting, or when the material thickness needs to be made uniform.

Surface-levelling parameters

Movement position relative to the X axis
Positive and negative values can be set.

Movement position relative to the Y axis
Positive and negative values can be set.

Movement distance
Indicates the distance between one cut and the next. Only positive values can be entered in this field. For surface levelling, it is recommended to set a “movement distance” of approximately 80% of the tool thickness.

Depth
Indicates how far to descend during the surface-levelling cycle relative to the acquired position.

Z step
Indicates the maximum downward step into the material. Depending on the levelling depth, the Z increment may decrease so that all passes are performed at the same depth.

Plunge cutting speed
Indicates the working speed on the Z axis during the automatic cycle, expressed in (mm/min).

Forward cutting speed
Indicates the working speed in the XY plane during the automatic cycle, expressed in (mm/min).

Change tool origin
Pressing this button switches between the saw-blade origin calculated using the line laser and the core-drill origin calculated using the cross laser.

Executing the machining operation

The “SURFACE LEVELLING” program does not require the X, Y and Z origins to be reset.
The tool position when the cycle is started is used to determine the starting position.
After setting the various parameters, move the running saw blade to the maximum required depth in the worktable or material and start the cycle using the CYCLE START button.

NOTE

The program can be used with the “A” axis inclination set to ZERO degrees or NINETY degrees, allowing tools such as saw blades or milling cutters to be used.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.5 EXCAVATION

The pocketing page is used to machine a rectangular pocket with filleted corners and a flat bottom.
A suitable milling cutter mounted on the main spindle is required for this operation.
The “worktable level” is used as the bottom level.
The cycle uses multiple passes, with a helical entry at the centre and a pass spacing that can be set in the parameters.

Parameters

X
Length of the pocket to be machined.

Y
Width of the pocket to be machined.

Fillet R
Size of the fillet required at the corners of the rectangle.

NOTE

A value greater than the milling-cutter radius must be entered in this field.

Pocket depth
Total depth of the pocket in the material.

Z step
Indicates the maximum penetration step into the material. Depending on the pocket depth, the Z increment may decrease so that all passes are performed at the same depth.

Pass spacing
Indicates the lateral movement between one pass and the parallel pass. A pass spacing equal to 60% of the milling-cutter diameter is recommended in order to avoid movements over the corners.

Entry depth increment
Indicates the depth increment achieved by one turn of the helix during the material-entry procedure.

Machining speed
Indicates the programmed linear machining speed. Set a value suitable for the material, tool type and thickness to be cut.

Downward speed
This speed is used during the entry procedure.

Reset X and Y axes
Resets the X- and Y-axis origin at the bottom-left point shown in the image.

The position is acquired by placing the centre of the milling cutter at the indicated point.
For machines equipped with a “pointing laser”, the positions can be acquired using the position indicated by the laser.

Executing the machining operation

Enter the X, Y and R dimensions that define the shape of the required rectangular pocket.
Check that the tool data, particularly the diameter, are correct.

The following two execution modes are available

Mode for reaching the pocket down to the worktable position

To machine a pocket correctly, position the machine centre at the pocket origin as shown in the figure in the previous chapter. This ensures that the entire operation is performed correctly relative to the designated area.

Then set the dimensions that define the shape of the pocket to be machined.

Before starting machining, verify the accuracy of the selected tool data, paying particular attention to the diameter, as this directly affects the accuracy and quality of the pocket.

The “worktable position” must be acquired with reference to the bottom level of the pocket. To determine it correctly, position the tool on the top edge of the material and reset the Z position. Then move downwards by the required pocket depth. The worktable position can now be acquired using the dedicated button. When using milling cutters, it is advisable to perform this operation with the A axis at 90_ to avoid inaccuracies caused by the actual tool length.

After defining the worktable position, reset the X and Y axes. Press the relevant reset button and position the centre of the milling cutter exactly at the point indicated in the figure by the reference symbol. On machines equipped with a pointing laser, the X and Y zero point can be acquired directly using the laser reference.

The pocket depth depends directly on the level set as the worktable position and on the Z-axis position when the cycle is started using the “Cycle Start” button. Machining begins with a helical entry at the centre, down to the depth specified by the “Z Step” parameter. The area is then cleared using a concentric movement according to the spacing set in the machining parameters.

The machine movements required to reach the initial position are performed at the “clearance position”, which can be defined in the tool parameters. This ensures that the tool does not interfere with any obstacles during positioning movements.

Mode for positioning above the piece and resetting the origin value

This mode requires the ”Pocket depth” parameter to be set and then used.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.6 CUTS

This function can be used to add multiple cuts.
This special cut type creates a series of parallel cuts in the same group, with the option of having two groups, each with its own configurable direction.
The interface appears as follows:

Sidebar

Cut-group selection and management

Create first cut group
Cuts are created parallel to the machine's current position.
The direction in degrees for the first cut group is shown below the button.

Create second cut group
The second cut group is created in the same way as the first, except that its direction can be different. The direction in degrees for the second cut group is shown below the button.

Cut management
In this mode, certain changes can be made to the cuts before they are executed. Cuts can be edited, disabled, moved or deleted, and pauses can be added before execution.

Cut parameters

For each of the two cut groups available to the operator, up to 100 simultaneous cut configurations can be entered with their respective parameters.

Orthogonal directions
If the two cut groups have mutually orthogonal directions, the first green icon is displayed immediately below the cut-group selection and management buttons. Otherwise, the second red image is displayed.

Width

The distance between one cut and the next.

Number

The number of parallel cuts to be created.

Cut position
These buttons are shown beside each cut configuration and allow the operator to decide whether to position the cuts from the saw-blade position towards the motor, or in the opposite direction, moving away from the motor.

Show next/previous cuts
Allows the operator to display all cuts in the selected group.
Changing the selected group returns to the first page of the group, where the first four cut configurations are displayed.

Stretching Cuts

The operator can extend all cuts in the first and second groups at the start or end of the set length.

Start
This parameter extends the cut at its starting end.

End
This parameter extends the cut at its final end.

Delete and update cuts

Delete cuts
Clicking this button allows the operator to delete the created cuts and start again with a new arrangement.

Update cuts
Pressing this button moves the cuts to the correct position relative to the machine.

C axis

The machine head can be rotated to adjust the orientation of the cuts in both the first and second groups.

Rotate _90
Pressing the button rotates the machine head by 90_ from its current position.

Rotate -90
Pressing the button rotates the machine head by - 90_ from its current position.

Machine-head rotation
This parameter specifies the machine-head rotation angle (in degrees).

MDI
Pressing this button rotates the machine head according to the value set in the previous parameter.

Thickness

The operator can define the thickness of the slab to be cut.

Manual thickness
The operator can enter the slab thickness manually.

Thickness measured by machine
The operator can acquire the thickness using the machine by moving the machine height to the required position and selecting the button. The distance between the worktable and the saw blade is used as the material thickness.

Executing the machining operation

The operator can configure both cut groups by changing their respective parameters.
Once the required result has been obtained, press the “Cycle Start” button to perform the machining operation.

First cut group

One or more sets of cuts are defined in the first cut group by changing the Width, Number and Cut Position parameters, as well as the C-axis rotation.
In the following operation, cuts have been set parallel to the machine's current position.

Second cut group

As with the first cut group, the parameters of the second group can be changed to obtain the required result.
In this operation, the cut direction has been changed to create cuts orthogonal to those in the first group.

Cut optimisation and management

In this section, the cut execution order can be changed and each cut can be enabled or disabled.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.7 ISOCAM

IsoCam is the software used to perform profile cutting with a saw blade. It allows profiles to be drawn or imported, the path to be selected and different machining methods to be applied.
Job programming is divided into several stages, which are described in the following paragraphs.

When IsoCam is opened, if no previously created job exists, the operator can create a new one starting from the first machining step.
If a previously created job exists, it is loaded automatically and the operator is taken directly to the final machining step:

Elements shared by the various steps

The user interface consists of several areas.

  • Menu: quick utilities.

  • Top bar: functions specific to the active page.

  • Central area: contains the drawing or active area according to the page.

  • Sidebar: window containing the parameters to be edited.

  • Bottom bar: buttons generally available in different areas of the software.

NOTE

All these elements vary according to the operating context.

The following elements remain visible at all times, regardless of the current stage of the process.

Menu

The menu bar is located at the top, above all other elements of this interface.

View

Provides the operator with settings relating to the visibility of pieces in the work area.

Options

Colour-related settings can be changed.

Language

ISOCAM is currently available in the following languages:

  • German

  • English

  • Spanish

  • French

  • Italian

  • Portuguese

Right-hand sidebar

Settings
Opens the settings panel in the centre of the page.

Info
Opens a small panel containing useful information and contact details.

Step Management
This section can be used to move forwards and backwards through the different steps of the workflow.

Close
Pressing the button closes the IsoCam program.

Machine settings

This panel can be used to switch to IsoCam Advanced mode, return to the basic version, and change the X and Y Grid Step values.

Bottom bar

New job
Opens a new blank IsoCam window and resets the workflow to Step 1 of 4.

Open job
Opens a previously saved job.

Save job
Saves changes made to a job.

Edit job
Returns the workflow to Step 1 of 4, allowing changes to be applied to the current job.

Section drawing (step 1 of 4)

The first programming stage consists of drawing the section to be machined. The window provides the standard controls of CAD software: draw line, draw arc, snap, move, etc.
The underlying concept of the software is to create the section as a quick sketch, which is then edited entity by entity using the dedicated controls. Drawings in .dxf format generated by external CAD systems can also be imported at any time.

Top bar

Draw Line command
Enables/Disables the line-drawing command.
When enabled, it creates a new line starting from the end point of the last entity entered, if available; otherwise, the line is generated at the selected point.

Draw Arc command
Enables/Disables the arc-drawing command.
When enabled, it creates a new arc starting from the end point of the last entity entered, if available; otherwise, the arc is generated from the selected point.

Move selected segments
After selecting an entity, press this button to move it within the work area.

Mirror Shape
After selecting an entity, this button can be used to flip it horizontally and/or vertically within the work area.

Fillet
After enabling the function, follow the parameters on the right.

Invert active selection
Inverts the active selection when the button is pressed.

Delete selected segments
Deletes the selected entities.

Right-hand sidebar

Line properties

When a line is selected in the work area, the right-hand column is updated to show the properties of the selected entity, which can be edited by the user:

Length

Indicates the linear distance between the two ends of the selected line, calculated from their coordinates in the workspace.

Angle

Indicates the orientation of the line relative to the horizontal axis of the reference system.

Δx

Indicates the change in the X coordinate between the start and end points of a line or entity, i.e. the horizontal distance travelled relative to the X axis of the reference system.

Δy

Indicates the change in the Y coordinate between the start and end points of a line or entity, i.e. the vertical distance travelled relative to the Y axis of the reference system.

Extend/Shorten selected line
Extends or shortens the selected line by a specified amount, changing its length while keeping its angular direction unchanged. The change is defined using the dedicated input field.

Round Angle
Automatically rounds the line angle to the nearest multiple of 90_ (0_, 90_, 180_, 270_), making it easier to align with the orthogonal directions of the reference system.

Scale connected segments

Applies proportional scaling to all entities directly or indirectly connected to the selected line.
When this option is active while the line is being extended or shortened, spatial consistency between the connected elements is maintained, preserving their relative positions in the preview.

Arc properties

When an arc is selected in the work area, the right-hand column is updated to show the properties of the selected entity, which can be edited by the user.
The arc can be defined in several ways: by points, by centre, radius and arc, etc.
The various properties are shown in the window on the right.
A property can sometimes be changed in different ways, for example by changing the radius or the start/end point. The “Fixed centre” flag is used to select the method of modification.

Radius

Indicates the constant distance between the centre of a circular curve or arc and any point on its circumference.

Start/end angle

Angle of the start or end point relative to the centre.

Tangent to Previous / Next

Changes the start or end angle so that the arc is tangent to the previous or next entity.

Fixed centre

Determines the effects of a change to the radius or angle.

Translate / Move selection

When the “move” command is enabled, the movement parameters window appears. Movement can be performed directly by clicking in the drawing area (including with snaps active) or by setting the parameters.
Confirm the movement using the “OK” button.

Position selector
Moves by the set “Delta” value in the direction of the arrow.
The centre button resets the movement.

Translation
Total movement relative to the initial position.
The numbers in the boxes on the right are used for the “array copy” command.

Move copy

When enabled, this function creates a copy of the selected entity and applies the movement only to the copy, leaving the original entity unchanged.

NOTE

This command is visible only when the values in the second column of the “Translation” parameter are 1.

Mirror

After enabling the command, set the centre of symmetry by clicking in the work area or entering the coordinates, select the mirror direction and press the “OK” button to confirm.

Centre of symmetry

Changes the coordinates of the centre of symmetry used to flip the selected entity horizontally or vertically.

Coordinates to invert

Indicates whether to flip horizontally, vertically or in both directions.

Mirror copy

When enabled, the mirroring operation creates a mirrored copy of the selected entity while leaving the original unchanged.

Fillet

A first message displayed in the right-hand column allows the operator to set the fillet radius and confirm the selection.

A second message informs the operator that fillets can now be inserted between two lines; this remains available until the function is disabled.

The following example shows fillets applied to two adjacent lines and to a line adjacent to an arc:

After applying the fillets:

Bottom bar

Import DXF file
Imports a DXF file. There are no restrictions on the file format, but small files in R12 format are recommended.

Export DXF file
Exports the drawing in DXF format.

Undo change
Undoes the last command performed.

NOTE

The keyboard “Esc” key performs the same function.

Start/end snap
Makes it easier to select the start or end point of an arc or line.
When the cursor approaches a vertex, the nearest point is highlighted by a yellow box containing an X and the vertex coordinates.

Ortho command
Enables/Disables the “Ortho” command to keep segments orthogonal.

Connected Segments command
Enables/Disables the “Connected Segments” command. The start point of the next segment is the end point of the previous segment.

Drawing grid
Enables/Disables the grid in the drawing window. The grid parameters can be accessed using the settings button.

Undo Zoom
Restores the previous zoom level.

Select area for Zoom
Selects a focus area for zooming.

Reset Zoom
Restores the original zoom level.

Profile selection (step 2 of 4)

The section drawn previously must be applied to a suitable profile.
The profile can be linear or curved, in the X/Y plane or vertical; certain machining modes are enabled or disabled according to the selection. For example, a curved profile in the XY plane can be machined only with a vertical saw blade, while the opposite applies to a curved profile in the XZ or YZ plane.
The profile type is selected using the buttons on the left, the parameters used to define the profile geometry are shown at the top centre, and a preview of the result is shown at the bottom centre.

Central area

Linear Profile

Set the direction and length.
The sign of the “Delta Z” value follows the Z axis (positive upwards, negative downwards).

Arc Profile

Define the direction, working plane, concavity and geometric properties.
Any change to the geometric properties affects other variables.

NOTE

The maximum radius that can be set is 9999mm.

Circular Profile

This is machined externally only, using a horizontal saw blade.

Linear Profile parameters

Profile Execution

Two modes are available: “Along X” and “Along Y”.

Line length (L)

Horizontal length of the base of the inclined segment, measured between the starting point and the horizontally projected end point.

End-point Delta Z (H)

Height of the inclined segment, i.e. the difference in position between the start and end of the segment.

Arc Profile parameters

Profile Execution

Select either “Along X” or “Along Y”.

Machining orientation

Select either “XZ Plane” or “XY Plane”.

Machining type

Select either “Concave” or “Convex”.

Length (L)

Horizontal distance between the two ends of the arc, i.e. the chord connecting the start and end of the arc.

Starting radius (R)

Distance from the centre of the arc to a point on the arc itself. This determines the overall curvature of the arc.

Vertical rise (H)

Maximum height of the arc relative to chord L; this is the vertical distance between the highest point of the arc and the chord.

Angle span (A)

Central angle subtended by the arc, expressed in degrees.

NOTE

Changing any of the following values: “Length”, “Starting radius”, “Vertical rise” or “Angle span” automatically recalculates the remaining parameters.

Circular Profile parameters

Starting radius (R)

Defines the radius from the starting point.

Guard

This flag indicates whether the C axis rotates during machining (guard enabled) or remains stationary at C=0_ (guard not present).

Bottom bar

Table view
Enables/Disables the table view.

Additional lights
Enables/Disables additional lights for the 3D view.

Default view management
Changes the viewpoint.

The page is divided into panels containing the different types of data to be set for machining.

Tool parameters

The operator can define the tool parameters:

For a new project, the data are loaded automatically according to the tool physically installed. For a previously saved job, the tool data are those already saved in the previous program.

Shows the name of the selected tool.

Maximum diameter of the saw blade, measured from one end of the toothed edge to the other.

Measures the distance between the inner edge of the tooth of the saw blade currently mounted on the machine and the C rotation axis.

Safety distance between the saw blade and the worktable.

RPM (Revolutions Per Minute)

Linear Profile

For linear profiles, machining can be performed with the saw blade vertical or horizontal (from the front or from the left).

Vertical Orientation

Horizontal Orientation

Machining type

Vertical Orientation

Horizontal Orientation

Machining type

Machining can be performed in two modes:

Cut mode
Performs mutually parallel cuts that follow the selected profile.

Scraping mode
Performs mutually parallel cuts transverse to the profile direction.

Cut-mode configuration

Mutually parallel cuts are performed following the selected profile, with the distance between cuts taken from a parameter.

Step

Indicates the distance between a cut position and the adjacent cut. If it is greater than the saw-blade thickness, material remains between the passes.

Start / end extension

Extends a cut at its start/end by the set value.

Auto Plus

Enabling this flag automatically increases the extension value according to a value established by the system.

Excess material

Thickness of material to be left above the required final section.

Cut direction

The cut can run from right to left or from left to right, depending on the selected configuration.

Scraping-mode configuration

The movement is transverse to the profile direction and is used for surface finishing of the piece.

Scraping step

Indicates the distance between one transverse movement and the next along the profile direction.

Cutting speed and mode

Depending on the previous selections, different menus appear for selecting the parameters required to define the machining operation.

If the selected machining type is Cut-Mode Configuration, two types of machining parameters are available:

Marble Mode
The cut is performed in a single pass.

Granite Mode
The cut is performed in steps.

Marble Mode

General parameters:

Cut in both directions (finishing)

This flag allows a return speed different from the forward speed to be set.

Never raise (finishing)

WARNING!

When this parameter is enabled, the saw blade must emerge completely from the cutting section.

Speed parameters:

Forward

Execution speed of the forward pass.

Return

Execution speed of the return pass.

Penetration

Execution speed during pass penetration.

Minimum

When a non-zero value is set, the cutting speed depends on the cutting depth. Movement is therefore performed at the forward speed for cuts at zero depth and at the minimum speed when the cut reaches the maximum depth for the selected section.

Granite Mode

General parameters:

Forward cutting removal

Amount of material removed during the forward pass.

Return cutting removal

Amount of material removed during the return pass.

If the selected machining type is Scraping Configuration, a single machining parameter is available:

Machining speed

Sets the speed at which scraping machining is performed.

Machining parameters (advanced)

Machining parameters (advanced)
This button opens the advanced machining parameters window.

This screen can be used to check and edit various parameters, many of which were set in steps 2 and 3.

The first operation is to select the profile type to be used:

Then set the following parameters:

Machining

Machining can be performed vertically or horizontally.

Along X or Y.

Machining Data

The following parameters can be set for a Linear profile:

Profile inclination (mm)

Defines the profile inclination by specifying the difference in height between the end point and the start point.

For an Arc profile, the parameters set in the previous steps are available.

Both profiles also share the following machining data:

Step

Fixed in Y: maintains a fixed distance between cuts regardless of the underlying section.

If the “Step” value is less than the “Thickness” value, the step is optimised on horizontal lines.

Selects whether or not to perform a cut at the start of the profile. The depth of this cut can be set using the adjacent box.

Perform cut at end

Selects whether or not to perform a cut at the end of the profile. The depth of this cut can be set using the adjacent box.

Tool Data

This section shows data set previously and other tool-specific parameters.

Tool description

Tool magazine
Opening this panel allows the tools to be managed: new tools can be created, existing tools edited, their order in the list changed, or tools removed.

Position No.

A preview of the calculated cuts is displayed according to the previous selections. The page is divided into several areas containing controls for managing changes.

After checking the cuts or making the required changes, press the “NEXT” button to open the page used to generate the cutting program.

Menu

In the fourth step, an additional item becomes visible in the top menu:

Cuts

This menu provides the operator with quick settings for the generated cuts.

Top bar

NOTE

Some buttons remain disabled until a cut is selected.

Regenerates the cuts using the default settings.

NOTE

Edit cut position
Changes the position of the selected cut.

Add leading cut to separate pieces

Add cut at mouse position (Ins)

Central area

Cut sequence number
For each selected cut, the sequential cut number, spatial coordinates of the edges and contact status of the edges with the entities are displayed, indicating whether one or both are in contact.

General Data

Cut Data

Bottom bar

Cut options
Alternative to right-clicking to display cut options.

Move/extend cuts
Alternative to the keyboard arrows for moving/extending cuts.

Shift
Alternative to the keyboard Shift key.

Program creation

After preparation in the fourth step is complete, the final stage can be opened. This displays the result and generates the ISO file.
The central area shows a 3D view of the generated machining operation, taking the operating mode into account. Click in the area to rotate the view and control the zoom.

NOTE

Basic procedure

Step 1

To begin, press the "New job" button. Make sure the "Connected Segments" function is active, then enable the "line" command. Click repeatedly in the work area to draw the required section. When the drawing is complete, click the "line" command again to disable it. Then select each entity individually to check and, if necessary, edit its parameters.

Step 2

In this step, the operator can set basic general parameters relating to the required machining type.

Step 3

The tool parameters and the type, orientation and parameters of the selected machining operation can now be set.
The “Machining parameters (advanced)” panel also provides an overview of all parameters set up to this point.

Step 4

A cut list is generated automatically for the current machining operation. Cuts can be inserted, edited and removed according to operating requirements.

ISO Generation

The final machining step allows the operator to create an ISO file from the resulting job or restart the procedure.

DOC2.8 POLISHING (OPTIONAL)

The Polishing program can perform polishing using different machining types. The method used to acquire the slab geometry can also be selected: either by detecting the points that define the surface vertices (from three to a maximum of six) or by using a regular surface (rectangle) and entering the zero position and the values of the two sides.

Machining modes

To use this machining operation, first select one of the two available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

NOTE

The ‘
Rectangle selection
' and '
Free point selection
’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Switch to Free point selection mode
Pressing the button shown switches from the operating mode that uses a rectangle as the predefined shape to the mode in which the surface is acquired by selecting points.

Switch to Rectangle selection mode
Pressing the button shown switches from the operating mode in which the surface is acquired by selecting points to the mode that uses a rectangle as the predefined shape.

Entry/exit mode

The buttons shown switch tool entry and exit between progressive and standard mode.

NOTE

The ‘
Progressive
' and '
Standard
’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Switch to progressive mode
When this mode is enabled, at program start the machine moves from the working Z position to the safety Z position, then moves towards the first point of the surface to be polished (for a rectangle, the top-left point). It then moves along the surface perimeter, progressively lowering the Z position so that the tool reaches the working position at the end of the path. The machine then performs a polishing operation around the perimeter, after which the selected operations are performed in sequence. At the end of the work sequences, the machine makes another pass around the perimeter of the surface to be polished, then follows the same path while progressively raising in Z until the safety position is reached at the end of the path.

Switch to standard mode
When this mode is enabled, at program start the machine moves from the working Z position to the safety Z position, then moves towards the first point of the surface to be polished (for a rectangle, the top-left point). It then lowers in Z to the working position while keeping the X and Y axes stationary, after which the selected polishing operations begin. At the end of the set work sequences, the machine moves to the first point of the surface to be polished and then rises in Z to the safety position.

Free point selection mode

This mode is displayed as follows:

Parameters

Point positions

Set
This button enters the coordinates of each point. When the position has been acquired, the adjacent figure changes from red to green.

NOTE

A minimum of three and a maximum of six points can be entered.

Clear
This button deletes all saved positions if the setup is incorrect and the points need to be acquired again.

Machining types

Perimeter
Polishing is performed only around the perimeter of the set geometric shape.

Horizontal passes
Multiple horizontal passes are performed.

Vertical passes
Multiple vertical passes are performed.

Global repeat
The machining cycles can be restarted by entering the number of repeats in the relevant box. The box in the “Completed” column shows the number of repetitions completed for the entire machining operation.

Machining parameters

Repetitions

Each machining type can be repeated the number of times set in this field.
If the value is set to “0”, that machining operation is not performed.

Completed

Displays the number of repetitions completed.

Step [mm]

Indicates the distance between one pass and the next, selectable for each machining type.

Polishing tool parameters

Machining speed
Indicates the speed at which machining is performed.

Downward speed
Indicates the required positioning speed along the Z axis to the selected coordinate.

Tool wear
Allows tool wear to be taken into account during machining by entering the compensation value.

Executing Free point selection mode

WARNING!

Between one operation and the next, the machine moves without rising to the safety position.

The operator sets the positions of a minimum of three and a maximum of six available points by moving the machine manually and using the corresponding save controls. After the points have been defined, configure the machining parameters for each required polishing type. The specific parameters of the tool used for polishing are set at the same time.

At any time before starting the polishing cycle, the operator can change the tool entry and exit mode by selecting one of the two available options.

After configuration is complete, the machine's A axis must be inclined to 90_ and saw-blade rotation started. The operator can then execute the programmed cycles by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. During execution, progress can be monitored in the “Completed” column, which shows the cycles completed for each selected polishing type.

Rectangle selection mode

This mode is displayed as follows:

Parameters

Rectangle position

Rectangle sides
The shape on which machining is performed is defined by the values assigned to Y and X, which correspond to the sides of the rectangle. The coordinates of the lower-left vertex of the rectangle are acquired using the respective reset buttons below each axis. Both values must be reset.

Machining parameters

See the Free point selection machining parameters mode for the following operations: Perimeter, Horizontal/vertical passes and Global repeat.

Zigzag
Zigzag passes are performed.

Polishing tool parameters

See Free point selection saw-blade parameters for the following saw-blade parameters: Machining speed, Downward speed and Saw-blade wear.

Y-axis step for Zigzag
For zigzag polishing mode, the Y machining step can be changed, allowing the working path to be divided into multiple passes. If the value is left at zero or set higher than parameter B, the polishing step along the Y axis is equal to B.

Executing Rectangle selection mode

WARNING!

Between one operation and the next, the machine moves without rising to the safety position.

The operator defines the position of the rectangle to be polished by moving the machine manually and changing the corresponding coordinate values. Once the rectangle has been defined, configure the machining parameters for each required polishing type. The specific parameters of the tool used for polishing are set at the same time.

At any time before starting the polishing cycle, the operator can change the tool entry and exit mode by selecting one of the two available options.

After configuration is complete, the machine's A axis must be inclined to 90_ and saw-blade rotation started. The operator can then execute the programmed cycles by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. During execution, progress can be monitored in the “Completed” column, which shows the cycles completed for each selected polishing type.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.9 PROGRAM LIST

The ISO Program List page allows multiple programs, previously created using CAD-CAM software, to be run consecutively on machines with two work areas, Twin machines, or when multiple jobs are created while the machine is already running.

Top bar

The top bar shows information for monitoring list progress.

Enable/Disable ISO Program List
This button, located at the top right of the ISO Program List panel, enables/disables the function.

List execution status
Indicates whether the list is currently running.

List progress bar
Shows the progress and execution status of the list.

List progress bar

This progress bar provides information on the execution status of the current ISO program, while also giving an overview of the next program in the list and the program that has already completed machining and moved to unloading.

In the previous image, no program is yet shown in unloading because list execution has not started and no piece has been processed. Conversely, if there is only one ISO file in the list, or if machining has started and all other files have already been executed, the Next section is empty.

During execution, program progress is displayed in real time, as shown below.

Side menu

The right side of the suction cup panel contains buttons for managing individual files in the program list.

Execute next program
Moves directly to execution of the next program in the list.

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upwards in the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down
Moves the selected ISO file downwards in the list of files to be executed.

Delete selected item
Removes the currently selected item from the list.
If multiple items are selected, only the first selected item is deleted.

Suction-cup panel
Opens the suction-cup management panel.

Suction Cup Panel

The suction cups can be operated manually to move pieces from one work area to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable/disable suction cups
The screen shows a top view of the suction cup assembly divided into its different zones. Pressing a zone changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is configured to generate a vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is configured for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Park suction cups
Pressing the button retracts the suction cups to their rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
Pressing the button lowers the suction cups from the parking position to the limit stop. Make sure there is enough space for the suction cups to extend fully.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
Pressing the button lowers the Z axis until the material contacts the work surface, switches off the vacuum pump and activates blowing from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
This control brings the suction cups into contact with the material, activates the vacuum pump in the areas marked green and blowing in the areas marked red. When the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blowing control
The button switches blowing on or off from the suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, making sure that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that the material has no defects or breaks that could create hazards or cause machine malfunctions.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom button has no effect on the vacuum pump, which continues to operate. The pump can be forced off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, a dedicated sensor checks the vacuum status. If an adequate vacuum level is not detected, the “vacuum failure” alarm appears. The pump remains active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes the vacuum to drop rapidly, resulting in the material lifted by the suction cups falling.

Bottom bar

The lower part of the bar displays functions relating to execution of the ISO program list, together with tool and slab monitoring information.

List execution management

The lower section also contains the two buttons for selecting program execution modes:

Manual / automatic
Defines whether the machine status is manual or automatic.

Single / automatic next
Defines whether the next program starts automatically.

Slab and tool monitoring

In the centre and on the right of the bottom bar, the operator can configure periodic tool diameter monitoring by setting checks at intervals based on the number of cycles performed.

Number of Cycles Between Saw-Blade Probes
Specifies the number of cycles between one saw-blade probing operation and the next.

Number of Cycles Until Next Probe
Indicates the number of cycles remaining before the next saw blade probing operation.

Tool diameter
Shows the saw-blade diameter value.

Slab thickness
Displays the slab thickness.

ISO Program List Execution

If the ISO Program List is disabled, the switch at the top right of the panel appears off. The function can be enabled simply by clicking this button.

The ISO program list is expanded automatically as ISO programs are generated in Parametrix. The operator can nevertheless reposition items within the list or remove them as required.

Before executing the list, the operator can set the number of cycles to be performed between tool probing operations.
The number of cycles remaining until the next probing operation is then updated and displayed.

The operator starts execution of the program list by pressing the “Start cycle“ button. The programs are then executed in sequence, simultaneously displaying the current program, the program to be executed next and the program already completed.

If the program execution mode is set to Manual and Single, list execution stops at the end of the current program, immediately after preparing the next program to be executed.
The operator can then press the Next button when appropriate and resume execution by pressing the “Cycle Start” button again.

DOC3 PARAMETRIX

The system has been designed to help the operator program automatic cuts. The software can be used to:

  • Define the position of the slab in the machine work area and create the material perimeter for machining

  • Create pieces using parametric shapes

  • Import shapes created with other CAD systems

  • Generate a list of pieces to be machined

  • Find the best position for the pieces on the slab

  • Set special cutting functions

  • Program the cutting sequence and create the machine movements

  • Monitor cutting execution on screen

Work area and piece list

The following is a typical representation of the Parametrix work area, with the imported-piece list already populated and an acquired image of the slab.

Inserted piece list

When a piece is created, the program adds it to the piece list. From the list, pieces can be placed in the work area, modified, and the number of pieces still required for the job can be checked.

Piece positioning

Parametrix allows pieces to be positioned within the machine work area in order to create the cutting file.
Once the slab has been acquired, its perimeter created and the pieces for the job created, the pieces must be imported onto the slab. Pressing the button in the piece table places the piece in the work area. It is possible to work with 1 or more pieces at the same time.

If the pieces are not completely inside the slab, a warning/danger symbol appears in the top-left corner.
This symbol indicates that problems may occur when managing the cuts; however, no program function is disabled.
