DOC3.1.3.1 CREATING CUTS FROM DXF DRAWINGS

The machine can perform cuts, milling operations and holes from drawings created with CAD software and saved in “.dxf“ format, automatically recognising certain machining operations to simplify and speed up the work of the machine operator.

NOTE

For Parametrix to interpret this information, certain conventions must be followed when creating the drawing:
All drawn pieces must be closed and converted into polylines forming a polygon.
To insert the piece mark for identification, it must be placed inside the polygon.

Parametrix settings for recognising imported layers

To open the customisation settings window for DXF file import, press the User Parameters button on the Parametrix top bar.
Then go to the section for managing Layer names.

For each listed function type, the user can assign a name (corresponding to the Layer name set in the CAD software used) and assign certain default-value parameters for specific machining operations.

Function

Layer Name

Miter cuts

Miter cut

Downstand

Downstand

Backsplash

Backsplash

Offset

Offset

Cuts under the material

below

Drip system

Gocciola

Milling

Milling

Rim

Rim

Drilling

Drilling

Additional cut

Added

Anchoring hole

keil

Chamfer

Chamfer

Lower Chamfer

Lower Chamfer

Deactivate

Deactivate

Remove

Remove

Buttons

The buttons to the left of each machining operation can be used to:

Information window
Displays a graphical representation of the information required to create a Layer associated with the machining operation.

Download example
Downloads a DXF file containing an example of a Layer associated with the machining operation.

Miter Cut mode

Certain conventions must be followed to insert a miter cut automatically:

  • Miter cuts can only be inserted on piece sides; if the miter cut does not apply to the entire section, the side can be divided into several parts.

  • A miter cut can be applied to external arcs (e.g. a circular table or curved backsplashes, but only on the external cut).

  • For internal arcs (e.g. curved backsplashes), the cut is performed in passes; the saw blade is tilted automatically to avoid collisions with the material.

For users of CAD systems, the procedure requires creating a Layer with the following properties:

Layer Name

Inclinato _ (followed by the number identifying the required inclination angle).

NOTE

The inclination is expressed in degrees.

Example

Inclinato45 or Inclinato-45

When a negative value is entered, the inclination refers to a diverging cut; when the value is positive, the cut converges towards the inside of the polygon.

Downstand mode

The downstand function is a machining operation used to obtain a rectangular piece with the same length as the line set as the reference side.

To insert the cuts automatically when creating a downstand, create a Layer named “Alzata” and then enter the height.

Layer Name

Alzata _ (followed by the downstand height).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Alzata100

In Parametrix, this automatic function creates a new piece whose width is equal to the length of the line identifying the side of the required downstand. The two sides to be bonded together are cut at the same inclination, ready for a mitred-joint finish.
The inclination associated with these sides can be set using the adjacent parameter.

Degrees

Sets the inclination used when importing the inclined sides of the machining operation.

Backsplash mode

The backsplash/downstand function is a machining operation used to obtain a rectangular piece with the same length as the line set as the reference side.

Similarly, to insert the cuts automatically when creating a backsplash, create a Layer named “Rivestimento” and then enter the height.

Layer Name

Rivestimento _ (followed by the backsplash height).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Rivestimento150

In Parametrix, this automatic function creates a new piece whose width is equal to the length of the line identifying the side of the required backsplash, without a miter cut and ready for a square-corner finish with edge gripping.

Offset mode

The offset function is very useful when extra material must be left beyond the finished piece dimensions. By drawing lines on the required sides, the functions associated with those sides are automatically shifted in the correct direction.

To insert the required extra material automatically, create a Layer named “Offset” and insert all the lines corresponding to the sides to which the setting must be applied automatically.

Layer Name

Offset _ (followed by the number identifying the offset value).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Offset3

Lower Cut mode

The lower cut function is only available on machines fitted with the optional mechanical equipment that allows a cut to be made below the visible surface of the slab.

To insert a lower cut automatically, create a Layer named “Sotto” and insert a line representing the cut.

Layer Name

below

Example

below

NOTE

The length of the resulting cut also depends on the saw blade diameter and material thickness set in Parametrix.

Drip System mode

The drip system function inserts a cut whose width is greater than the saw blade thickness and whose depth is less than the material thickness.

To insert a drip groove automatically, create a Layer named “Gocciola” and insert a line or arc representing the centre of its width.

Layer Name

Gocciola _ (followed by the number identifying the drip groove width).

NOTE

The width is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Gocciola10

The drip groove depth is then determined by the dedicated parameter.

Pocketing

Depth of the cut associated with the drip groove. This value is ignored if the user sets a value in the DXF file.

The cut depth can be managed automatically using the dedicated Parametrix parameter, or the user can set a value by entering the character “&” followed by the required depth.

Layer Name

Gocciola _ (drip groove width) _ & _ (drip groove depth).

NOTE

The depth is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Gocciola10&5

NOTE

The length of the resulting cut also depends on the saw blade diameter and material thickness set in Parametrix.

NOTE

For curved drip grooves, a single cut is made with the saw blade outside the arc.
Any parameters specified in the Layer name are ignored.

Milling mode

Certain conventions must be followed to insert an automatic milling operation.

If a milling geometry is created for one or more sides of the external polygon, the milling cutter performs the machining operation outside the drawn perimeter. This also applies to a single perimeter side. If the entire perimeter is to be cut with the milling cutter, any saw blade cuts are removed.

The cut depth can be defined by creating a dedicated Layer.

Layer Name

Fresatura _ (followed by the number identifying the milling depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Fresatura10

If no depth value is specified in the “Fresatura“ Layer name, the thickness of the current machining operation is used.

Another available function is the insertion of a polyline (open or closed, such as a circle or a single path made up of a linear polyline) to mill a shape within the larger perimeter.

Recess / Flush-Mount mode

The recess/flush-mount function is a machining operation used to recess a perimeter, usually to install appliances or sinks.

To insert the required recess automatically, create a Layer named “Ribasso”.

Layer Name

Ribasso _ (followed by the number identifying the recess width).

NOTE

The width is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Ribasso20

The recess depth is then determined by the dedicated parameter.

Pocketing

Recess depth. This value is ignored if the user sets a value in the DXF file.

The recess depth can be managed automatically using the dedicated Parametrix parameter, or the user can set a value by entering the character “&” followed by the required depth.

Layer Name

Ribasso _ (recess width) _ & _ (recess depth).

NOTE

The depth is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Ribasso20&3

NOTE

The fillet radius between the perimeter sides cannot be modified by the user; it is determined by the milling cutter radius.

The recess can be machined along a closed path that does not overlap the piece sides; in this case, the area inside the drawn perimeter is milled.

Drilling mode

The drilling function allows Parametrix to add drilling operations to pieces.

To insert a drilling operation automatically, create a Layer named “Foratura” and draw a circle where the hole is to be made.

Layer Name

Foratura _ (followed by the number identifying the hole depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Foratura5

If the depth is not specified, the hole is applied using the thickness of the material currently used by Parametrix.

In basic mode, the circle radius corresponds to the radius of the tool currently set in Parametrix.

Additional Cut mode

The additional cut function allows Parametrix to add a cut.

To insert an additional cut automatically, create a Layer named “Aggiunto” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the additional cut is to be created.

Layer Name

Aggiunto _ (followed by the number identifying the distance at which the cut is to be added).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Aggiunto50

The cut is added inside the piece (where material is present) or outside the piece (where no material is present), according to the sign of the distance:

  • If the distance is positive, the cut is added outside the piece.

  • If the distance is negative, the cut is added inside the piece.

When an additional cut is applied to internal cuts, for example a cut-out, the cut is added inside the piece, where no material is present.

Anchoring Hole mode

The anchoring hole function allows Parametrix to add anchoring-hole machining operations to pieces.

To insert an anchoring-hole machining operation automatically, create a Layer named “Keil” and draw a circle where the anchoring hole is to be made.

Layer Name

Keil _ (followed by the number identifying the anchoring-hole depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimetres.

Example

Keil5

In basic mode, the circle radius corresponds to the radius of the tool currently set in Parametrix.

Chamfer mode

The chamfer function allows Parametrix to add chamfer machining operations to pieces.

To insert a chamfer machining operation automatically, create a Layer named “Smusso” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the machining operation is to be created.

Layer Name

Smusso _ (distance along the X axis) _ & _ (distance along the Y axis) _ & _ (inclination angle).

NOTE

The measurements are expressed in:
X: millimetres
Y: millimetres
A: degrees

Example

Smusso10&10&45

If the three values are not geometrically compatible, the machining operation is not applied.

Lower Chamfer mode

The lower chamfer function allows Parametrix to add lower-chamfer machining operations to pieces.

To insert a lower-chamfer machining operation automatically, create a Layer named “Becco” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the machining operation is to be created.

Layer Name

Becco _ (distance along the X axis) _ & _ (distance along the Y axis) _ & _ (inclination angle).

NOTE

The measurements are expressed in:
X: millimetres
Y: millimetres
A: degrees

Example

Becco10&10&45

If the three values are not geometrically compatible, the machining operation is not applied.

Deactivate mode

The deactivate function allows Parametrix to deactivate cuts on pieces.

To insert a deactivate function automatically, create a Layer named “Disattiva” and draw a new line over the line representing the side to be deactivated.

Layer Name

Deactivate

Example

Deactivate

Remove mode

The remove function allows Parametrix to remove cuts from pieces.

To insert a remove operation automatically, create a Layer named “Rimuovi” and draw a new line over the line representing the side to be removed.

Layer Name

Remove

Example

Remove

Hole mode

The drilling function allows Parametrix to recognise every circle within the piece area whose radius is smaller than the “Maximum core drill radius” parameter.

Holes can be inserted freely in all Layers (except those identified as neutral).

An additional core-drill option removes an island of material left attached after the saw blade cuts have been made. For Parametrix to apply this option, one or more circles must be drawn so that they intersect the sides of the island cut with the saw blade. The “Automatic holes distance” parameter is then used to position a series of holes calculated automatically according to the material remaining to be cut after the saw blade operation.

Managing neutral Layers

To retain parts of a drawing in the DXF file that must not be treated as cuts or other functions managed by Parametrix, they can be assigned to Layers recognised as neutral.

Create the Layers using the names assigned in the Neutral Layers (1,2,3) fields on the “Layer Names” page of the Parametrix user parameters. The “*” character means that all imported Layers with the same text before and after the “*” symbol are ignored during import.

Examples

WorkingDetails.dxf

VeinDirections.dxf

Top.dxf

Kitchen_WithLayout.dxf

Kitchen_Curve.dxf

BookMatch_Wall.dxf

BookMatch_Floor.dxf

Bathroom.dxf

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.1.3.2 COLOURING LAYERS

This function can be used to colour one or more cuts on pieces created from DXF files.

Buttons

Change layer colour
Press the button on each row to change the colour associated with the corresponding layer.

Procedure

To associate a colour with the cuts of a piece:

  • Create a Layer in the CAD software;

  • Assign a colour to it in the dedicated Parametrix panel;

  • Draw a line (or curve) over the line representing the cut to be coloured within the Layer.

Once the piece is imported, the cut over which the line was drawn in the Colour Layer is displayed in the colour set in Parametrix (not the colour set in the DXF file).

NOTE

The line drawn over the cut to be coloured must completely overlap the line representing the cut.

Example

In this example, two cuts on the piece are to be coloured. The “ColoreE“ Layer was created, and lines were added over those to be coloured.

As shown in the Parametrix work area, the cuts take on the colour associated with the Layer in the imported DXF file.

DOC3.1.3.3 DYNAMIC TAGS

This function can be used to assign configuration parameters to DXF file Layers.

Parameters

The parameters are:

Name

Defines and identifies the Layer name.

Entity Type

Defines the type of entities to be displayed.

LineWeightMethod

Selects the method used to determine the line thickness.

LineWeight

Defines the thickness of the lines belonging to the Layer.
This thickness is applied when LineWeightMethod is set to “ByConfiguration“ mode.

ColorMethod

Selects the method used to determine the Layer colour.

Color

Defines the colour of the entities belonging to the Layer.
This colour is applied when ColorMethod is set to “ByConfiguration“ mode.

Buttons

Create configuration
Creates a parameter configuration for importing a Layer.

Delete configuration
Deletes a parameter configuration for importing a Layer.

In this example, the characteristics of the elements drawn on the “Venature“ Layer are to be modified.

The entities are imported according to the parameters set in the dedicated window.

DOC3.1.4 SUCTION CUPS

This section sets the piece movement speed when using the suction cups.

Parameters

XY speed

Sets the speed at which the piece is moved by the suction cups.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Z speed

Sets the Z-axis speed at which the piece is moved by the suction cups.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Rotation speed

Sets the rotation speed of the piece when using the suction cups.
This value is expressed in degrees per minute.

XY unloading speed

Sets the speed at which the piece is moved by the suction cups during piece unloading or lower cutting.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Z unloading speed

Sets the Z-axis speed at which the piece is moved by the suction cups during piece unloading or lower cutting.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

NOTE

The XY unloading speed and Z unloading speed options may or may not be available.
These options are normally selected when the program is installed, according to the customer’s machining requirements.
Contact Donatoni Support to change these options.

DOC3.2 NEW JOB

This button completes the current job and starts programming the next one.

Execution procedure

A job ends when the machine cutting program is generated or when the piece status is saved.
This button clears the slab and pieces from the work area, leaving it available for the next job.

A message appears requesting confirmation before creating a new job.

WARNING!

Confirming deletes:
the slab photograph and perimeter;
all pieces in the work area (including commercial pieces);

DOC3.4 SLAB MACHINING PARAMETERS

When the “Slab Parameters” panel is opened, the machining parameters screen is displayed, allowing the operator to manage machining data.
Machining data can be set and edited using the parameters panel.

Selected-material management

The top section of the “slab machining parameters” panel contains elements for managing materials:

The elements that make up this section of the slab machining parameters are described below.

Selected Material
Shows the name of the currently selected material.

Create new material button
Pressing this button opens a window for creating a new material.
The relevant window is shown below.

Button Open Materials Management panel
Pressing this button opens a window for managing the available materials.
The relevant window is shown below.

Selected-material thickness
This field shows the thickness of the selected material.
This value is essential for all calculations performed by the program.

Add a new material

This small graphical window is used to compose the name of a new material:

If creation of the new material is confirmed, it is selected automatically.
The material parameters and thickness are updated accordingly.

Open the materials management panel

Materials can be managed from this panel:

Search bar
The text bar immediately to the right of this icon can be used to apply search filters based on the names of the available materials.

Remove filter
This button is enabled only after a filter has been applied; pressing it removes the applied filter.

Remove material
This button deletes a material from the list.
A material can be deleted only if it is not the currently selected material (shown and highlighted in the first image in this section).
An additional confirmation pop-up allows the material to be deleted.

Duplicate material
This button duplicates the material selected in the list and its associated parameters.

Edit material
This button edits the parameters of the material selected in the list.

Machining-type selection

Selecting the machining type controls the contents of the parameter-management window.

For each machining type, its preview shows the selected increment mode, the forward cutting speed (plunge/entry speed for Hole machining) and the tool diameter.

Pass type

Full-depth pass
A Full-depth Pass performs the entire machining operation in a single pass. The tool therefore enters the full thickness of the material immediately and performs the operation.

Step / spiral pass
These passes do not enter the full material thickness immediately, but do so gradually.
The machining operation is therefore repeated at different heights until the worktable position (end of the material) or the selected height is reached.

Machining types

Linear

Full-depth pass

Step pass

Increment parameter description

Forward
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when the machine cuts in the direction of saw-blade rotation.

Reverse
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when cutting in the direction opposite to the tool direction.

Final
Indicates the cutting depth of the final tool pass through the material. This cut is always performed in the direction opposite to saw-blade movement.

Speed parameter description

Plunge
Determines the speed during tool penetration into the material.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Forward
Indicates the required speed for the forward cutting phase.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Reverse
Indicates the required speed for the return cutting phase.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Final
Indicates the speed that the machine must maintain during the final cutting pass.
This value is expressed in millimetres per minute.

Accelerate cuts
If this parameter is set to a value greater than zero, the saw-blade rotation speed is increased progressively from the start of the cut up to the specified distance.
The remainder of the cut is then performed at full speed.

Decelerate cuts
If this parameter is set to a value greater than zero, the saw-blade rotation speed is reduced progressively from the set distance before the end of the cut until the cut is completed.

NOTE

For increments and speeds, the “Reverse” and “Final” parameters may both be present, neither may be present, or only one may be present.
These options are normally selected when the program is installed according to the customer's machining requirements.
To change these options in order to use a different machining method, contact Donatoni Support.

Arc

Step pass

Miter cut

Full-depth pass

Step pass

Increment parameter description

Cut with probing (enabled / disabled)
If enabled, two slab-probing measurements are taken at the ends of the required cut before the miter cut is executed and their average is calculated.
This value is used during miter cutting.

Milling

Full-depth Pass

Step pass and spiral pass

Hole

Full-depth pass

Step pass

Executing machining with a step pass:

  • The machine approaches the material at maximum speed until it reaches the distance from the material specified in the APPROACH parameter.

  • The number of steps is calculated as:

    • Material thickness divided by step thickness

      • rounded up if necessary

  • The machine starts moving at machining speed.

    • If the ENTRY STEP parameter is set (non-zero and greater than zero), the machine operates at the speed set in the second ENTRY field until it reaches the distance set in the ENTRY STEP field.

  • The machine performs the steps calculated in the second point at the Step speed.

  • After each step (including the first), the machine returns to the material position at maximum speed, then moves at maximum speed to a short distance before the start of the next step.

  • If the EXIT STEP parameter is set (non-zero and greater than zero), the machine operates at the speed defined in the second STEP field until it reaches the distance defined in the first EXIT field.

    • The remainder of the step is performed at the EXIT speed.

Description of Hole parameters with step pass

Approach position
The machine approaches the material at maximum speed until it reaches the distance from the material set in this parameter. From this point, the core drill starts moving at machining speed.

Step
These parameters define the thickness of the machining steps and the machining speed. The number of machining steps is calculated from the machining-step thickness and the material thickness.
For example, if the user sets this parameter to 3 mm for material with a thickness of 20 mm, the hole is performed in 7 steps.

Entry
If this value is set to a value other than 0, an interval is defined from the first step and, where applicable, for the following steps, during which the machine operates at a speed different from that defined in “STEP”.

Exit
If this value is set to a value other than 0, an interval is defined from the final step and, where applicable, for the preceding steps, during which the machine operates at a speed different from that defined in “STEP”.

Pause after
If this parameter is enabled, the machine pauses after each hole is completed so that the operator can check for material residue trapped inside the tool.
The operator must press the START button again to resume the program.

Change of cutting parameters

The parameters described previously for the saw blade, milling cutter and core drill can be changed if the user is authorised to use them.

To select the tool whose parameters are to be changed, press the “Select tool” button on the right-hand side of the panel.

Change cutting parameters
Opens the screen for changing the cutting parameters of the selected tool.

Pressing this button displays a window containing a saved parameter configuration for each available material. The results also depend on the selected machining type.

A “Change Cutting Parameters” window similar to the following example image opens:

At the bottom left of the “Change Cutting Parameters” panel is an initially empty text bar that can be used to apply a search filter.
The button to the right of the bar is enabled only when the bar contains text and a search filter is therefore applied. Pressing it clears the filter and empties the text bar.

Bottom bar

The bottom bar of the Slab Parameters panel appears as follows:

This bar consists of the following elements:

Saw-blade preview
Shows the saw-blade tool currently mounted on the machine.

Milling-cutter/core-drill preview
Shows the milling cutter or core drill currently mounted on the machine.

Tool Panel

DOC3.5 MANUAL CONTROL ACCESS

This panel provides access to certain manual machine controls.

Buttons

0_ - 90_
Rotates the C axis to 0 or 90 degrees.

Parking
Moves the machine to the parking position.

Probe Slab
Any point on the slab can be selected; probing is performed at that point.

CRF Cycle
This button starts the procedure for calculating the CRF.

Washing cycle
Manually starts the washing cycle for a piece or the entire worktable.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the tool.
The button colour indicates the water status: White = Off; Blue = On.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The button colour indicates the water status: White = Off; Blue = On.

Slab probing cycle

The probing cycle calculates the slab thickness and acquires the worktable position using the dedicated probe mounted on the machine.
To start it, enable the button on the manual controls panel, then press a point inside the slab in the work area.
A symbol appears at the selected position, indicating where probing is to be performed.

When the machine has completed the cycle, a panel opens showing measurements obtained by probing the slab.

This information includes:

Thickness

Measured slab thickness.

Worktable position

Position of the worktable.

Slab position

Position measured on the top surface of the material placed on the worktable.

The data collected by the probing cycle can be saved using the following buttons:

Set slab thickness
Saves the slab thickness measured during the probing cycle.

Set worktable position
Sets the value measured during the probing cycle as the worktable position.

Start probing
Restarts the probing cycle at the same indicated position.

CRF (Flange Rotation Centre) measurement cycle

The CRF cycle measures the distance between the inner edge of the tooth of the saw blade currently mounted on the machine and the C rotation axis.
To start it, enable the button on the manual controls panel, then press a point inside the slab in the work area.
A symbol appears at the selected position, indicating where the saw-blade cuts used to measure the CRF are to be performed.

WARNING!

Cuts are performed in the material during this cycle.
The operator must therefore carefully select the position on the slab at which the cycle is started to avoid damaging it.

The machine performs two parallel cuts with the A axis at 0_: the first with the C axis at 0_ and the second with the C axis at 180_.
At the end of the procedure, the operator is asked to use a tape measure or calliper to measure the internal distance between the two cuts on the slab.
This measurement must then be entered in field “A” of the panel that opens at the end of the cycle.

The measurements must be entered in the relevant field:

A

Internal distance between the two cuts performed on the slab during the cycle.

CRF (A/2)

Measurement of the saw-blade Flange Rotation Centre. It is calculated as half the internal distance between the two cuts on the slab.

The data collected during the CRF measurement cycle can be saved using the following button:

Set CRF measurement
Sets the value calculated by the CRF cycle as the CRF measurement for the saw blade currently mounted on the machine.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.6 LASER MANAGEMENT

This panel is used to add or remove laser references in the work area.

Buttons

Line-laser reference
Adds the line-laser reference to the work area according to the machine position.

Draw cross laser
Adds the cross-laser reference to the work area according to the machine position.

Delete all drawings
Deletes all lines and crosses added to the work area in this mode.

Delete individual drawing
Allows the operator to delete a laser element drawn in the work area by clicking it.

Line laser

The line laser is a tool aligned with the saw blade mounted on the machine. It is used to collect information relating to the position and orientation of the saw blade on the worktable.

To acquire the reference, move the machine to the required point and press the button to detect the line-laser direction and add the reference to the work area.
Using multiple references makes it possible to identify the perimeter and position of the slab or a piece on the worktable.

NOTE

There is no limit to the number of references that can be saved.

Cross laser

The cross laser is used to collect information relating to the position of the laser pointer on the worktable.

To acquire the reference, move the machine to the required point and press the button to detect the cross-laser position and add the reference to the work area.
Using multiple references makes it possible to identify the perimeter and position of the slab or a piece on the worktable.

NOTE

There is no limit to the number of references that can be saved.

DOC3.8 SLAB PERIMETER

To operate, the program must know the edge of the slab to be machined. This function traces the perimeter.

Perimeter creation modes

The program allows the operator to draw the perimeter using one of the following modes:

Rectangle mode
Creates rectangular perimeters.

Point mode
Creates polygons of any shape.

NOTE

The creation mode can be changed at any time while creating the perimeter.
When switching from “point” mode to “rectangle” mode, the perimeter is converted to a rectangle and all polygon vertices are lost.
Confirmation is requested before the operation proceeds.

Rectangle

This mode creates rectangular perimeters.

To change the size and position of the rectangle, drag the yellow circles in the work area or change the values in the bar below.

Dimensions

X-axis and Y-axis dimensions of the perimeter.

Position

Coordinates of the lower-left vertex of the rectangle relative to the lower-left corner of the worktable.

For points

This mode creates polygons of any shape.
To do this, the operator can position the points that form the perimeter as required, as shown in the figure below.

In this mode, the perimeter can be edited using the following buttons:

Close perimeter
After all required points have been acquired, pressing this button closes the perimeter.

Remove last point
To edit a closed perimeter, press this button to open it.
Continuing to press the button removes previously created points in reverse order.

Once closed, the perimeter turns blue and its vertices are indicated by yellow circles.
During both the creation phase and after the perimeter has been closed, the vertices can always be moved in the work area to improve accuracy.

Bottom bar

The operator can interact with a perimeter in the work area using the buttons in the lower section of the screen.

Snap to cross laser
Allows the operator to move the perimeter vertices to the positions of any laser crosses in the work area.
Dragging a vertex near a laser cross snaps it to that position.

Move perimeter
Moves the selected perimeter to a new position by interacting with it in the work area.

Create a new perimeter

The program allows more than one perimeter to be created for positioning the pieces to be machined.
Areas of the slab in which no pieces can be placed can also be defined.

Perimeter
Creates a perimeter within which pieces can be placed.

Avoid area
Defines the perimeter of an area in which pieces cannot be placed.

Delete perimeter
Enables individual deletion mode, allowing the operator to delete one or more created perimeters by clicking them.

The created perimeters are shown in the list at the top right. To edit a perimeter, select it in the work area or select the corresponding entry in the list.
The currently selected perimeter has blue outlines and yellow vertices; the remaining perimeters can also be distinguished by colour: green for slab perimeters and orange for avoid areas.

NOTE

Two or more slab perimeters cannot overlap.

This screen can be used to add stress-relief cuts to the slab.

Slab trimming
Adds stress-relief cuts to the slab perimeter.

NOTE

Each created perimeter can be trimmed differently.

To complete perimeter creation, the operator is asked to enter information about the machining operation to be performed.

Thickness

The operator must enter the thickness of the slab on the worktable.

Name

Name to assign to the slab job.

Customer

Indicates the name of the customer for whom the job is being performed. This field is optional.

Job

Indicates an identifier for the job. This field is optional.

NOTE

The slab thickness and job name are mandatory fields and must be entered before confirming the perimeter.
The additional-property information below is optional.

Avoid areas

Avoid areas are areas of the slab that the operator does not want to make available for positioning pieces.
Reasons may include breaks in the material, unattractive veins, or the need to preserve certain parts of the slab.
They are represented as blue areas in the work area.

When the Nesting function is used, the pieces are arranged so that none of these areas is occupied.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.8.1 SLAB TRIMMING

Slab trimming is a function that adds stress-relief cuts to the job. These cuts trim the slab along its edges.
The function can be enabled in the perimeter creation panel.
The following example screen shows the four cuts, one per side, that can be inserted.

Sidebar

Slab trimming
To add/remove a stress-relief cut on the slab, select the corresponding side.
The Offset value specifies the distance of the trimming cut from the slab edge.

NOTE

Only slabs with a rectangular perimeter can be trimmed. This function does not operate in “by points“ mode.
Multiple perimeters can also be trimmed differently.

Executing the machining operation

In the work area, the program checks that the operator does not position pieces outside the slab trimming cuts.
Pieces can also be magnetically aligned to these cuts, as shown in the figure.

When the cutting program is executed, the machine performs these trimming cuts before any other operation. A trimming pause is then performed immediately afterwards, giving the operator time to remove the discarded slab material.
This allows subsequent slab movements using the suction cups to be performed without obstruction from the trimmed material.
These operations are also shown in the list on the cut management and optimisation screen.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.8.2 AUTOMATIC PERIMETER (OPTIONAL)

This function allows Parametrix to automatically determine the perimeter of a photographed slab.

Buttons

Automatic perimeter
Starts the calculation for automatically detecting the perimeter of the slab shown.

Using the automatic perimeter

To use this function, take a photo of a slab on the worktable or load an image from the computer.
The operator is then taken to the perimeter management panel.

In the right-hand section, press the button to calculate the automatic perimeter.

NOTE

Only one perimeter is calculated, assuming that the image contains a single slab.

At the end of the operation, the vertices of the calculated perimeter can be edited manually if they are not sufficiently accurate.

When the photo is opened, the data is analysed to set the perimeter, avoid areas and thickness correctly:

Horizontal

Total

DOC3.11 CREATING PIECES

Parametrix is designed to machine flat, closed geometric shapes representing pieces.

Import DXF file

DOC3.11.1 IMPORTING DXF FILES

In this section, pieces can be created by importing DXF files.

File list

The left-hand side of the window contains a list showing all folders and DXF files in the currently selected path.

The item at the top of the list

returns to the folder above the current folder.

Initially, the list shows the DXF files in the PC working folder. The folder can be changed using the dedicated buttons to the right of the file list.

USB storage device
Opens the USB storage device connected to the PC, allowing its folders to be browsed and its files to be displayed.

Working folder
Provides quick access to the PC working folder.

Browse folders
This button can be used to browse all folders on the PC.

Delete file
Switches to “Delete file” mode. In this mode, an eraser icon appears to the left of each file name in the list.
Selecting a file permanently deletes it.

Sorting and filtering the displayed files

The controls below the list apply filters and sort the displayed files.

A search bar at the top of the image can be used to filter files by name, displaying only those containing the entered text.

This area of the screen also contains the following buttons:

Clear filter
Clears the text entered in the search bar and removes the file display filter.

Sort by date
Sorts the files in the list by creation date. By default, they are sorted from newest to oldest. Pressing the button again sorts them from oldest to newest. The operation can be repeated to change the sorting order.

Sort by name
Sorts the files in the list by name. Pressing the button selects ascending or descending order.

NOTE

The name search applies only to files in the folder, not to any subfolders.
Conversely, sorting by name and date applies to every item in the list, although folders are always shown before files.

Preview

When a file is selected, a preview of the drawing appears in the box at the centre of the screen, allowing its contents to be identified immediately.

The preview can be manipulated by dragging its contents or by using the buttons to its right.

Zoom in
Zooms in on the preview.

Zoom out
Zooms out from the preview.

Reset view
Resets the preview to its initial view, in which the entire drawing is visible.

Additional buttons

The following buttons can also be used to perform additional actions.

Details panel
Opens the panel showing details of the selected DXF file.

Panel Details

If a file has been selected, the “Details Panel“ can be opened to view the DXF properties. Use the following button to the right of the preview:

When opened, the following panel is displayed together with the list of pieces in the selected DXF:

Layout visibility management

The top of this panel lists the layouts as check boxes that can be enabled or disabled as required:

The first item in this layout list enables or disables the display of all layouts.

Side panel

Visibility and padding buttons

In addition to the previously shown buttons for changing and resetting the zoom level, two new buttons are available:

Highlight selected piece
Zooms in on the piece selected in the polyline list.

Pan view
Allows the preview to be moved by interacting with the screen.

Polyline list

The centre-right side of the panel lists the pieces contained in the selected DXF as polylines.
Selecting one of the values in the list highlights the corresponding piece in the preview in yellow.

When the button next to each piece is pressed, the list of polylines making up the piece is displayed.
An individual DXF polyline can also be highlighted simply by selecting its row in the list:

Bottom buttons

These buttons are located at the bottom of the side bar.

Find previous open polyline
Scrolls towards the beginning of the list of open polylines in the selected DXF.

Find next open polyline
Scrolls towards the end of the list of open polylines in the selected DXF.

DOC3.11.2 CREATING RECTANGLES

Rectangular pieces can be created by entering their width and height and placing them in the list of pieces to be machined.

The program can also associate an identifying mark (or label) with each piece and set the number of repetitions for rectangles of the same size.

Parameter description

The following data is required to create rectangular pieces:

Number of pieces
Number of copies of the piece having the same dimensions.

Width
Width of the rectangle. It is measured in the unit shown to its right.

Height
Height of the rectangle. It is measured in the unit shown to its right.

Mark
Label added to the piece for identification. This parameter is optional, as it is not essential for creating the piece.

Additional buttons

The following side buttons can also be used to perform additional actions.

Single import
When this button is enabled, multiple separate pieces can be created with a quantity of one each, instead of one piece with multiple copies.

Dynamic Tag Top
Assigns the Dynamic Tag Top to one side of the rectangle.

To enable the function associated with a button, press the button. It is then highlighted in light green.

NOTE

The “Dynamic Tag Top“ buttons next to the width and height boxes are mutually exclusive. The Dynamic Tag Top can therefore be assigned to only one side of the rectangle.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.11.3 CREATING PARAMETRIC SHAPES

In this section, pieces can be created using predefined parametric shapes. To draw a shape, simply enter its characteristic values.

Parametric shape categories

With reference to the image above, the main categories of parametric shapes are shown in the left-hand column.

Rectangular shapes
Such as rectangles and squares, with or without internal cut-outs.

Quadrilaterals
Such as scalene trapezoids, also intended for kitchen worktops.

Triangular shapes
Such as regular and curved triangles.

Kitchen worktops
Various kitchen worktop shapes with internal cut-outs.

Sector shapes
Such as sectors and partial circular rings.

Elliptical shapes
Such as circles and ellipses.

Polygonal shapes
Such as regular and curved hexagons.

Bathroom shapes
Various curved shapes for bathrooms.

Stone or memorial shapes
Such as pentagons and Latin crosses.

Tables
Shapes such as rounded rectangles and irregular octagons.

Special shapes
Such as stars and arcs.

Preview and parameter values

Once a category is selected, the correct shape can be chosen in the next column to the right.
An image at the centre of the screen provides detailed guidance on the dimensions to be entered. To the right of the reference image, a preview of the shape being drawn is displayed and updated in real time whenever any of its characteristic values is changed.
As described in the previous sections, once the dimensions have been entered, a mark (or label) displayed on the piece in the work area can be specified, together with the number of copies and whether single import is to be used.
The following image shows an example of creating a kitchen worktop.

Creating internal cut-outs

To create internal cut-outs, press one of the internal rectangles in the central image. The window shown below opens, where the cut-out can be edited as required and then inserted into the original image.

Additional settings

Additional parameters

The following data is required to create rectangular pieces:

Number of pieces
Number of copies of the piece having the same dimensions.

Mark
Label added to the piece for identification. This parameter is optional, as it is not essential for creating the piece.

Additional buttons

Single import
When this button is enabled, multiple separate pieces can be created with a quantity of one each, instead of one piece with multiple copies.

Mirror
When enabled, these two buttons mirror the piece vertically and horizontally, respectively.

Reset
Returns the shape being edited to its original state.

Out-of-square piece bar

Some pieces can be created using angles that are not square (i.e. other than 90 degrees).
To use this option, use the bar above the central image, which contains all the editable versions of that image. Editable parameters are shown in green.

Mirror

Pressing the two dedicated buttons mirrors the result displayed on screen about the vertical or horizontal axis, respectively. This function adapts the display to the operating requirements or the type of job in progress.

The following are examples of horizontal and vertical mirroring:

DOC3.11.5 IMPORTED PIECE HISTORY

This function allows the operator to retrieve the history of created pieces.

Three different display modes are available for the pieces in this section:

Cut view
Displays the piece and its cuts.

For the following examples, five pieces (A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5) were imported from the DXF named “Kitchen_Curve“.

The cut dimension view highlights the external perimeter in black and displays the corresponding length near the centre of each cut on the perimeter.

The overall dimensions view does not highlight any cuts. Instead, it shows the maximum width and length of the piece.

Commercial pieces can be created in this section of the “Create Pieces“ panel. This type of piece has the following characteristics:

  • they are created with a large number of copies;

  • the width and height can be changed even after a piece has been placed in the work area.

Parameters

Width
Width of the rectangle. It is measured in the unit shown to its right.

Height
Height of the rectangle. It is measured in the unit shown to its right.

Mark
Label added to the piece for identification. This parameter is optional, as it is not essential for creating the piece.

Importing a commercial piece

To complete creation of a commercial piece correctly, use the following button:

Import commercial pieces
Confirms creation of the commercial piece and adds it to the list of pieces to be machined.

The creation procedure also updates both the commercial piece list on the left and the list of pieces to be machined on the right. The following example shows both updated lists:

DOC3.12 PIECE LIST

When one or more pieces are created and imported into Parametrix, the program adds them to the piece list on the right-hand section of the main screen.

Using the piece list, the operator can:

  • Place pieces in the work area;

  • Keep track of pieces already machined and those still to be machined;

  • Apply certain changes to pieces.

List items

Each row in the list represents a piece imported into Parametrix.

As shown in this image, a row contains the following information about the piece:

Shape preview

Simplified representation of the piece geometry.

Piece mark

Label added to the piece to identify it.

NOTE

If the operator does not select a mark during creation, the program identifies the piece using the name of the file (DXF or CSV) from which it was imported, or the side dimensions if it is a rectangle.

Number of inserted and total pieces

Indicates the number of pieces in that row that have been inserted into the work area and the total number of pieces of that type that can be inserted.

Insert pieces into the work area

The following button in each row of the list is used to insert pieces into the work area:

Insert pieces into the work area
Inserts the selected piece into the work area.

The selected piece has been positioned in the work area and the number of inserted pieces in this row has been updated.

NOTE

Once the maximum number has been reached, the “Insert pieces” button for that row disappears because all pieces in the row have been machined.

Operations on pieces in the list

The buttons below the list are used to manage the list elements. In particular:

Clear piece list
Deletes all contents of the piece list.

NOTE

Commercial pieces are not removed from the list.

WARNING!

All pieces in the work area linked to rows removed from the list are removed.

Hide/Show commercial pieces
Hides or displays list rows associated with commercial pieces.

WARNING!

Hiding rows associated with commercial jobs removes all pieces linked to them from the work area.

Delete piece
Allows individual pieces to be selected for deletion from the list.

Filter/Sort pieces
Applies a filter to the pieces in the list or sorts them according to different criteria.

Additional piece properties
The operator can assign and edit the additional properties of the selected piece.

Delete piece

This function deletes pieces from the list individually. After the button is pressed, the program asks the user to select the row to be deleted and replaces the arrow used to insert pieces into the work area with an eraser.

Pressing this button deletes the corresponding row and therefore all the pieces it represents.

WARNING!

Deleting a row removes all pieces linked to it from the work area.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.12.1 FILTERING AND SORTING PIECES IN THE LIST

This function allows the operator to filter and/or sort the pieces in the list.
Pressing the button opens the following window.

Filtered piece list

Once criteria have been set for filtering or sorting the pieces, they can be applied using the button at the top right.

Enable/Disable
Applies/removes the filter and/or sorting to/from the pieces in the list.

Pieces that do not match the selected filter criteria are not shown in the piece list.

WARNING!

Pieces in the work area that do not meet the filter criteria are removed.


In the following example, only pieces with a height greater than 600 mm are to be shown and arranged in ascending alphabetical order.

Before applying the filter and sorting

After applying the filter and sorting

NOTE

The filtering and sorting function does not work with commercial pieces.
The filtering and sorting criteria are also respected by the nesting function.

Filtering pieces

In the upper section of this window, the operator can add a filter based on different piece characteristics.

As shown, the following buttons are available.

“Exclusion” filter application mode
Pieces must simultaneously satisfy the last logical condition created and the result of the previous conditions.

“Inclusion” filter application mode
Pieces must satisfy at least one of the last logical condition created or the result of the previous conditions.

Add filter
Adds the created logical condition to the filter list.

Delete filters
Deletes all filters from the filter list.

Creating a filter

To create a filter, select the property to be used from the first drop-down menu on the left.

After selecting the distinguishing characteristic, select a relational operator from the second menu.

Then enter a value appropriate for the property in the adjacent box to create a logical condition.

At this point, use the button to the right of the text box to decide how the filter being created interacts with any other filters in the list.

NOTE

In “Exclusion“ mode, a piece must satisfy
both
the logical condition being created and the result of the previous conditions.
In “Inclusion“ mode, a piece must satisfy the condition being created
or
the result of the previous conditions.

To complete creation of the filter, use the last button on this row. The filter is added to the list below.

Sorting pieces

In the lower section of the window, the operator can sort pieces according to certain properties.

After selecting an item from the drop-down menu, the following actions can be performed:

Ascending/Descending sorting
The operator can sort the pieces by a given category in ascending or descending order.

Delete sorting
The operator can restore the original order by deleting the previously selected sorting criterion.

Multiple sorting (Optional)

This function allows the pieces in the list to be sorted using more than one criterion.

In this mode, sorting criteria can be added using the following buttons:

Add sorting criterion
Adds a sorting criterion to the list.

Change position
Changes the position of a created sorting criterion in the list.

NOTE

The criteria in this list are applied from top to bottom.
This means that pieces are sorted according to the first criterion. If two or more pieces have the same value for the property linked to the first criterion, they are sorted according to the next criterion, and so on for every criterion in the list.


The following image shows an example of multiple sorting.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.12.2 ADDITIONAL PIECE PROPERTIES

This function changes the additional properties of a piece. These are details about the piece that can be displayed in different parts of the program and are also transferred to the ISO file generated for the machine.
Pressing the button and then the required row in the piece list opens the following window.

Property configuration

The centre of the panel lists the additional properties that can be assigned to a piece.

NOTE

The fields displayed in this window can be customised with the assistance of a Donatoni technician.

Buttons

The two buttons shown below are located at the bottom of the window:

Copy
Copies the additional properties of a piece.

Paste
Fills the additional property fields with previously copied data.

When confirmed, this information is associated with all pieces linked to the selected list row.

WARNING!

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13 EDIT PIECE

This panel allows the operator to apply different types of machining to a selected piece.
When it is opened, the following screen is displayed:

WARNING!

Some of the functions described in this section are also available on the Parametrix main page, but there is an important difference.
If a piece or cut is edited using the ‘Edit Piece’ panel, all pieces in the selected row are changed accordingly with the same machining operations.
By contrast, if machining is set from the work area, only the selected piece is changed.

Machining types

The “Edit Piece” panel can be used to apply one or more of the following machining operations, each of which is described below. In particular, Parametrix can:

Miter
Change the inclination of cuts, both under-square and over-square.

Drip system
Add a drip groove beside a cut.

Add
Add a cut parallel to one side of the piece.

Delete
Delete cuts from the piece.

Offset
Change the piece dimensions by applying offsets to its sides.

Hole
Add holes in the material, including to remove material that the saw blade could not cut.

Milling
Replace saw-blade machining operations with milling cuts.

Recess
Apply milled recesses. This is used, for example, to create sink cut-outs in kitchen worktops.

Lower Cut - (Optional)
Perform a cut on the lower surface of the piece using a dedicated mechanical option.

Downstand
Add upstands or lowered panels to the sides of the piece.

Kerb
Add a chamfered cut to one side of the piece.

Surface - (Optional)
Apply surface passes using vertical cuts and a horizontal saw blade.

Surface Levelling - (Optional)
Apply a surface-levelling cycle using vertical cuts and a horizontal saw blade.

Channel - (Optional)
Add a drainage channel to the piece using the saw blade.

Fillet
Round a vertex or side of the piece by applying a fillet.

Split
Cut the piece using a side or a custom line as a reference.

Internal cut-out
Add a rectangular, circular or elliptical internal cut-out to the piece.

Flutes
Create grooves by milling.

Maximum Envelope - (Optional)
Determine the maximum envelope of the piece.

Mirror
Create a mirrored version of the piece.

NOTE

Depending on the combination of options, some of these buttons may not be available.

Cut list

The cuts on the piece are displayed in the lower-left section of this panel.

A dedicated subdivision indicates whether a cut belongs to the external perimeter or to one of the internal perimeters. This classification makes it possible to show/hide the list of cuts belonging to a polygon by pressing the icon for the corresponding section.

As shown in the image, each row displays information about the cut it represents. In particular:

Manage machining
Button used to interact with the cut and apply the current machining operation.
On the main page, it enables/disables the cut.

Cut information

  • T - indicates the cut type (“Line”, “Curve”, “Milling”, etc.).

  • D - indicates the cut length.

  • I - indicates the cut inclination.

  • P - indicates the cut penetration.

Machining information

  • Machining type (“Linear”, “Arc”, “Miter”, etc.).

  • Pass mode (Full-depth pass or Step pass).

  • Cut feed speed.

  • Diameter of the tool used for machining (Saw blade, Milling cutter, etc.).

NOTE

This information changes according to the cut type. Not all information is always displayed.
For holes, for example, only penetration into the material can be displayed.

NOTE

If no cut is present on part of the piece, this is indicated by “None”.

Preview

The main part of the "Edit Piece" function provides the operator with a complete preview of the selected piece, showing all machining operations currently applied.

The displayed piece can be manipulated simply by moving the preview or by using the zoom controls to its right.

This section also contains other functions, which are described below.

Mark
Allows the mark of the selected piece to be changed.

Number of pieces
Allows the number of machined pieces and the total number of pieces to be changed.

Add favourite
The piece shown in the preview is added to the favourites list together with all changes applied when it is added.

Cut selection

A cut can be selected directly in the preview; its colour changes to yellow to confirm selection. Alternatively, select the corresponding row in the cut list in the bottom-left menu.

Clicking the green indicator to the left of each list element disables the corresponding cut.
The indicator turns red and the piece preview is updated, with the disabled cut changing to grey.
In the following example, the first two cuts in the external polygon of the piece have been disabled:

Bottom bar

This bar provides functions that make the Edit Piece operations easier to use:

Cuts
Displays the list of cuts on the piece.
This is the default view of the panel.

Sides
This button displays the lengths of the Piece sides in the list instead of the cut lengths. Selecting directly in the image or list highlights the selected piece side in yellow.

NOTE

Machining operations cannot be added to the piece in this mode.

History
Displays the history of operations applied to the piece.
It also allows the piece to be restored to the required operation.

Undo
Undoes changes made to the piece.
Pressing this button repeatedly restores the piece to its initial conditions.

WARNING!

The button works only while the “Edit Piece” panel remains open for the piece being examined.
If the panel is closed, the option to undo changes to that piece is lost, even if the panel is reopened.

Edit view
Enables or disables certain piece entities to improve visibility and make the piece easier to edit.

History

Displays all changes applied to the current piece and, if necessary, restores the current piece to a previous state.
If changes have been applied to the current piece, they are shown in the list on the left:

The menu on the left displays the machining states of the piece.

Machining state
Identifies a specific point in the machining history of the piece. It displays:

  • Name of the current piece;

  • Date on which the machining operation was applied;

  • Name of the machining operation applied;

  • Icon identifying the machining operation performed.

The unmodified state of the current piece is called "Default".
Selecting an item from the menu on the left displays the preview corresponding to the point at which that machining operation was applied.

Pressing the confirmation button restores the piece to the selected state. Any changes made after the selected state are removed.

At the bottom of the panel are three utility buttons for displaying the piece in the preview:

Show cuts
Shows the cuts on the shape.
This is the default active view.

Show dimensions
Shows the dimensions of each side of the shape.

Show angle
Shows an angle of the shape with its dimensions.

Edit View

This mode provides the operator with buttons that are visible only when “edit view” is enabled.

Each of the following buttons enables or disables one of the following piece elements:

Cuts
Shows/hides saw-blade cuts in the preview.

Holes
Shows/hides holes.

Milling operations
Shows/hides milling operations.

Recesses
Shows/hides recesses.

Cut arrows
Shows/hides the arrows indicating the direction of saw-blade cuts.

Piece name
Shows/hides the piece name.

Dynamic Tags
Shows/hides the piece Dynamic Tags.

Highlight Perimeter
Highlights the piece perimeter with a black line.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.1 MITER CUT

The ‘Inclination’ function defines a machining operation with the A axis at a value other than 0.
The interface for the “Miter Cut“ machining type resembles the following image:

Modes

NOTE

Selecting one square direction excludes the other.

Square direction _
When enabled, this mode allows the operator to create a miter cut with a positive angle.

Square direction -
When enabled, this mode allows the operator to create a miter cut with a negative angle.

Parameters

Degrees

This is the angle between the direction of the mounted tool and the surface of the material to be machined.
This angle determines the inclination at which the tool interacts with the material.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

After selecting the square direction, enter the required value next to it and select the cut to which the miter cut is to be applied.
When the machining operation is applied, the miter cut is displayed in a different colour.
Depending on the selected square direction, two different results can be obtained:

Square direction: Positive

In the following example image, a miter cut (45.0_) with positive square direction has been applied to every side except the internal arc, because a tool located inside the perimeter cannot be inclined.

Square direction: Negative

In the example image, miter cuts (45.0_) with negative square direction have been applied to the piece cuts in the reverse configuration to that shown in the previous section.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.2 DRIP SYSTEM

This function adds a cut with characteristics different from a normal cut.

The interface that opens resembles the following image:

Parameters

The cut width can be set (it must be equal to or greater than the saw blade thickness).

Distance from edge

Distance between the selected cut and the drip system operation.

Cut width

This is the width of the machining operation. The drip system can be wider than the saw blade thickness.
The program makes parallel cuts until the selected width is reached.

Cut depth

This is the plunge depth into the material.

Start distance

Inward distance at which the machining operation is created relative to the start of the cut.

End distance

Inward distance at which the machining operation is created relative to the end of the cut.

NOTE

Start distance and end distance can be enabled or disabled using the buttons to the right of the value.

Start Distance and End Distance

These parameters can be enabled or disabled using the buttons to the right of the value. When the buttons are grey (off), Parametrix ignores the parameters; when they are green (on, as shown in the figure), the program calculates the offset.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Based on the set machining parameters, a drip groove is inserted parallel to the selected piece cut.

The following image shows a drip groove operation created with the same parameters as the previous example.

In both examples, the machining operation was applied to the lower cut.

DOC3.13.3 ADD

This function adds a cut parallel to an existing cut at the required distance.
This machining operation can be applied to both straight cuts and curved arcs.

Parameters

To add a cut, the following parameter must be set:

Distance

Distance from the selected cut at which the parallel cut is added.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

After setting the distance parameter, select the cut relative to which the new cut is to be created.

The direction in which the new cut is added is calculated so that the piece is not damaged: outwards if an element of the external polygon is selected, or inwards for an internal polygon.
If the distance value is negative, the added cut is calculated in the direction opposite to the intended offset direction.

The following image shows the result of adding two cuts by selecting the two straight lines that define the recess in the kitchen worktop.

As shown, the new parallel cut is inserted in the Added Operations section and replicates the characteristics of the selected cut, such as its direction and machining type.

Button for adding cuts at concave corners

Applies an additional cut to each concave side.

DOC3.13.6 HOLE

This page can be used to drill a single hole at a specific position or a series of holes at a fixed distance.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first select one of the two available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

NOTE

The 'Hole in material' and 'Overcut removal' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Hole in material
The operator can create holes based on coordinates.

Overcut removal
Adds holes to the piece to remove saw blade waste.

Hole in the material

When this machining mode is selected, the currently selected vertex is highlighted in orange. Starting from this point, a preview of the hole to be added is projected, also shown in orange and generated according to the set parameters.

Parameters

Penetration

Specifies the depth to be reached by the machining operation.

X-axis distance

Distance along the X axis from the start point of the selected cut at which the hole is created.

Y-axis distance

Distance along the Y axis from the start point of the selected cut at which the hole is created.

NOTE

Relative to the selected point, the area to the right of the circle is considered positive for X and the area above the circle is considered positive for Y, as shown in the figure.

Executing Hole in Material

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

After selecting a vertex and setting the distance and penetration parameters, confirm the machining operation by pressing the green OK button.

Whenever a hole is successfully inserted in the material, the preview is updated and the hole is automatically added to the 'Additional Operations' section on the left:

NOTE

Unlike Overcut Removal, however, the centre points of arcs can also be selected. They are highlighted in the preview together with all other points that are valid references for inserting holes in the material.

Remove Disk's Material

When this mode is enabled, the selected vertex becomes the origin point of an orange preview consisting of multiple holes. Their size depends on the mounted core drill and their quantity is determined by the Hole distance parameter.

Overcut Removal parameters

Penetration

Specifies the depth to be reached by the machining operation.

Automatic hole distance

Sets the distance between the hole origin points.

Executing Overcut Removal

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Overcut Removal mode can be used between two consecutive cuts, whether both are straight, both are curved, or one is of each type.

The hole is added to the internal polygon list and identifies the overcut removal operation.
The following example shows Overcut Removal applied to two adjacent sides of the internal polygon:

Buttons available in Overcut Removal mode

Concave holes
Applies three holes to each concave corner.

Number of holes
Selects the number of holes to be inserted.

DOC3.13.7 MILLING

The ‘Milling’ function creates a milling operation on the piece, on a side, on an edge or along the entire perimeter.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

NOTE

One of the following modes must be selected

Vertex

Removes material that the saw blade cannot remove without damaging the piece. It is used only to finish specific points on the piece.

Side

The milling cutter is used to cut one side of the piece. It does not supplement the saw blade cut but replaces it completely.

Perimeter

Uses the milling cutter instead of the saw blade to cut an entire polygon of the piece. As in Side mode, it replaces the saw blade.

NOTE

In every mode, the cut width is equal to the diameter of the mounted milling cutter. Changing this value automatically updates the cuts to the new dimension.
In Vertex mode, changing the material thickness or saw blade diameter lengthens or shortens the cut so that it matches the newly selected dimensions.
If the milling cutter is too large to cut the selected side, an error message is displayed.

Thickness

Displays the slab thickness currently set in Parametrix to help the operator apply the machining operation.

Penetration
Normally, the penetration value is equal to the thickness. To change it manually, press the button shown on the left and an editable variable appears.

Milling at internal corners
Applies milling to internal corners.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

The effects of applying milling vary according to the selected mode and have certain differences, described in the following sections.
Milling starts from the approach point shown in the figure, identified by the solid coloured circle positioned at the origin.

Each milling operation applied to a piece is added to the cut list associated with a polygon and shown graphically in light blue.

  • In Vertex mode, the milling operation is aligned with the selected vertex.

  • In Side and Perimeter modes, one or all cuts of the polygon are replaced, respectively.

Execution on a vertex

The milling operation is applied to the vertex closest to the selected point on a cut in the preview.
It is applied between two consecutive cuts.

The following example image shows two vertex milling operations: the first on an upper-left vertex of the internal polygon and the second on a vertex of the external polygon.

Execution on a side

Selecting any point on a cut in the preview applies milling along the entire corresponding side.

The following image shows two side milling operations: the first on the left side of the internal polygon and the second on a lower side of the external polygon.

Execution on the perimeter

Regardless of the selected point or cut, milling is performed along the entire perimeter of the selected polygon.

DOC3.13.8 RECESS

The ‘Recess’ function adds a profile to the upper edge of the piece or kitchen worktop.
It is mainly used to lower the internal cut-outs of kitchen worktops by a specified amount so that a sink can be installed.
The tool used for this operation is the milling cutter.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

Plunge

Depth at which the cut is performed.
The maximum plunge value is the material thickness.

Distance

Specifies the required distance from the side of the piece. Positive, negative and zero values are permitted.

  • A neutral value (0) creates a recess at the same level as the polygon cuts.

  • A positive value positions the recess inside the piece, creating additional adjacent recesses if necessary.

  • A negative value positions the recess outside the piece, away from the polygon cuts.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

A recess is applied around the entire polygon of a selected cut, regardless of where the cut was selected.
The following is an example of a recess with a positive distance parameter value:

NOTE

If the recess distance is greater than the diameter of the milling cutter used, multiple adjacent recess passes are performed.
