DOC3.13.10 DOWNSTAND

This function creates a rectangular piece from the side of an object to form a downstand.

NOTE

This machining operation is available only for straight cuts.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first select one of the two available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

Backsplash mode
Creates rectangular pieces with all straight sides.

Downstand mode
In this mode, the two sides to be joined are inclined at the same angle.

Parameters

Height

Height of the downstand inserted when the machining operation is executed.
The width is determined in advance by the selected cut.

Miter piece sides

When enabled, automatically inserts miter cuts where cuts would otherwise collide.

Additional Downstand mode parameter

Degrees

This parameter is active only when Backsplash mode is selected.
It specifies the angle at which the machining operation is applied.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Clicking directly on the cut in the preview, or on the icon to the left of the cut in the corresponding list on the left where available, executes the selected machining operation.
Whenever a downstand or fillet is successfully applied to the material, the preview and the cut list on the left are updated.

Each piece created using this function is added to the Parametrix piece list.
The new pieces are also added to a list located immediately above the preview in the ‘Edit Piece’ panel;

This list can be used to select the required piece in the block and display its preview and cuts in the cut list.

Executing Backsplash

The following examples show the application of two backsplashes with the “Miter piece sides“ parameter enabled or disabled.
First, a backsplash 1000 mm high is applied to the lower side of the rectangle, followed by a second backsplash on its right side.

Miter piece sides disabled

No mitered sides appear in the result and the cuts of the original piece are not changed in the cut list:

Miter piece sides enabled

If the vertices of the new pieces, Piece_1 and Piece_2, are aligned, the sides sharing a vertex that are not adjacent to the original piece are replaced with miter cuts:

Executing Downstand

The following examples show the application of two downstands with the “Miter piece sides“ parameter enabled or disabled.
First, a downstand 50 mm high is applied to the lower side of the rectangle, followed by a second downstand on its right side.
In this mode, the original piece (Piece) and any generated pieces (Piece_1 and Piece_2) automatically receive miter cuts on all mutually adjacent sides.
The miter angle is determined by the degrees parameter.

Miter piece sides disabled

In this case, the adjacent sides between the original piece and the newly created pieces are automatically replaced with miter cuts.
The cut inclination depends on the set Degrees parameter.

Miter piece sides enabled

As in the previous case, miter cuts are inserted on sides adjacent to the various pieces, and their inclination depends on the value of the Degrees parameter.
In addition, when the “Miter piece sides” parameter is enabled, as with backsplashes, if the new pieces have aligned vertices, the sides sharing a vertex that are not adjacent to the original piece are automatically replaced with miter cuts.

Splitting pieces

When one or more pieces have been associated with the selected piece through Downstand or Backsplash operations, a dedicated button for managing the associated pieces appears at the top of the “Edit Piece” panel.

Split pieces
Separates downstands and backsplashes from the original piece.

Before splitting, the associated pieces are managed as a single unit within the work area. In this state, they form a block of multiple elements that undergo the same operations and have not yet been separated.

For example, when the original piece, a downstand or a backsplash is added to the work area from the piece list, all other associated elements are also inserted automatically.

When the Split Pieces button is pressed, each piece generated using a downstand or backsplash is disassociated from the original piece and treated as an independent item.

The associated-piece list previously shown above the preview in the Edit Piece panel and the Split Pieces button then disappear from the interface.

NOTE

When the pieces are split, each piece retains the miter cuts created during downstand or backsplash generation, together with all customisations and changes made while it was still associated with the original piece.

The following image shows the separate management of individual pieces that previously belonged to the same block.
In particular, only two of the three pieces have been placed in the work area (the original piece and the first piece generated by applying the first downstand), and the second piece has been repositioned and rotated without affecting the original piece:

WARNING

!
The piece splitting operation cannot be undone once executed.

DOC3.13.11 EDGE PROFILE

This function adds a chamfer, a lower chamfer (bird's beak), or both to the cuts of the selected piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

To use this machining operation, first select one of the three available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

NOTE

The ‘Chamfer’, 'Lower Chamfer' and 'Chamfer and Lower Chamfer’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the others.

Chamfer
Selecting this function performs the cut on the upper corner of the piece side.

Lower Chamfer (bird's beak)
Selecting this function performs the cut on the lower corner of the piece side.

Chamfer and Lower Chamfer
Selecting this function performs the cut on both the upper and lower corners of the piece.

The following parameters are common to both machining types:

X position

Distance along the X axis from the piece edge.

Y position

Distance along the Y axis from the piece edge.

Inclination A

Cut inclination angle expressed in degrees.

Inclination B

Cut inclination angle relative to the lower chamfer, expressed in degrees.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only in “Chamfer and Lower Chamfer” mode.

Thickness

Displays the slab thickness currently set in Parametrix to help the user apply the machining operation.

NOTE

This parameter cannot be changed directly from the Edge Profile section.

Perimeter

Enabling this parameter applies the machining operation to the entire perimeter of the piece.

NOTE

Square check boxes, initially disabled, are located next to the first three geometric parameters. One must be enabled to specify which parameter is to remain constant; when a second value is provided, the third is calculated automatically. A check box cannot be enabled if the corresponding parameter value is zero, in order to prevent geometrically inconsistent or invalid configurations.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

The edge profile operation can be performed only on straight cuts.

Whenever an edge profile is successfully added to the material, the preview is updated and the operation is automatically added to the 'Added Operations' section on the left.

Executing Chamfer

Side

The following image shows the edge profile operation applied to the upper corner of one side of the piece.
To apply the operation to the required side, click the side.

Perimeter

The following image shows the edge profile operation applied to the upper corner around the piece perimeter.
To apply the operation to the perimeter, enable the check box to the right of the label and then click a side of the piece.

Executing Lower Chamfer

Side

The following image shows the edge profile operation applied to the lower corner of one side of the piece.
To apply the operation to the required side, click the side.

Perimeter

The following image shows the edge profile operation applied to the lower corner around the piece perimeter.
To apply the operation to the perimeter, enable the check box to the right of the label and then click a side of the piece.

Executing Chamfer and Lower Chamfer

Side

The following image shows the edge profile operation applied to the upper and lower corners of one side of the piece.
To apply the operation to the required side, click the side.

Perimeter

To apply the operation to the perimeter, enable the check box to the right of the label and then click a side of the piece.

DOC3.13.12 SURFACE MACHINING (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to machine the material surface.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first select one of the two available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

NOTE

The 'Rectangular surface' and 'Zigzag surface' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Rectangular surface
The machine performs parallel passes across the surface.
The saw blade is used for this operation.

Zigzag surface
The machine performs zigzag passes across the surface.
The milling cutter is used for this operation.

Parameters

C-axis rotation

Sets the machining orientation, which can be horizontal (0_) or vertical (90_) relative to the work surface.

NOTE

The '0_' and '90_' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Pass extension

Each cut generated by this machining operation is extended at both the start and end by the length specified by this parameter.

Cut depth

Specifies the machining depth in the material.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Executing Rectangular Surface

After setting the machining parameters, select a side of the piece on which to perform the operation.
The cuts are performed from bottom to top.

Executing Zigzag Surface

After setting the machining parameters, select a side of the piece on which to perform the operation.
The cuts are performed from bottom to top.


Slab machining parameters

The operator can change the parameters for surface machining operations from the slab machining parameters panel.

Rectangular surface

This screen shows the machining parameters for “Rectangular surface“ mode.

Parameter description

Distance between forward passes
Distance between a forward pass and the following return pass.

Distance between return passes
Distance between a return pass and the following forward pass.

Forward passes only
When enabled, all passes are performed in the forward direction, from left to right across the piece.

Return passes only
When enabled, all passes are performed in the return direction, from right to left across the piece.

Raise saw blade at end of pass
When enabled, the saw blade is raised at the end of each pass.

Piston pressure
Enables piston pressure on the material and sets its intensity.

NOTE

The parameters for passes in a specific direction are mutually exclusive.
If either one is enabled, the program also enables raising of the saw blade at the end of the pass.

Speed parameter description

Plunge
Sets the speed during the tool penetration phase into the material.

Forward
Specifies the required speed for the forward cutting phase.

Reverse
Specifies the required speed for the return cutting phase.

Zigzag surface

This screen shows the machining parameters for “Zigzag surface“ mode.

Parameter description

Distance between forward passes
Vertical distance between the start point and end point of a diagonal pass in the forward direction.

Distance between return passes
Vertical distance between the start point and end point of a diagonal pass in the return direction.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.13 SURFACE LEVELLING (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to level the surface of the piece.

Parameters

Pass extension

Each cut generated by this machining operation is extended at both the start and end by the length specified by this parameter.

Executing the machining operation

Starting from the slab thickness set in the material parameters, the piece is machined as follows to reach the target thickness set in the machining parameters:

  1. First, parallel cuts are performed from left to right at the distance set in the parameters, using the linear-cut parameters.

  2. Cuts are then performed along the Y axis to create a grid, again using the linear-cut parameters.

WARNING!

The initial slab thickness must be set as the material thickness (probing can then be added for greater accuracy).
The target thickness is set in the machining parameters and is referenced to the worktable position.

NOTE

This machining operation can also be performed on commercial pieces.

Slab machining parameters

The operator can change the surface levelling parameters from the slab machining parameters panel.

Levelling cut parameters

Parameter description

Distance between horizontal passes
Distance between two parallel passes in the horizontal direction.
The button selects whether the passes are performed from top to bottom or vice versa.

Distance between vertical passes
Distance between two parallel passes in the vertical direction.
The button selects whether the passes are performed from left to right or vice versa.

Levelling position
Sets the required material thickness after levelling.

Rotate tool 90 degrees
When enabled, surface levelling is performed with the A axis at 90_.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.14 CHANNELS (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to add a channel in an area of the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

Distance from edge

The operator must enter the required distance in mm from one of the piece edges.
To position the channel against the edge, leave the value at 0; otherwise, enter the required distance.

Cut width

The operator must enter the channel machining width in mm.

Cut depth

The operator must enter the channel machining depth in mm.

Start Distance

The operator can enter the distance in mm from the channel reference cut.

End Distance

The operator can enter the distance in mm from the piece reference cut for the channel.

Automatic drip grooves

The operator can decide whether drip grooves are created automatically on the piece after the channel is created.

Thickness

Material thickness.

NOTE

Start distance, end distance and automatic drip grooves can be enabled or disabled using the buttons to the right of the value.
When disabled, Parametrix ignores them; when enabled, the program calculates the offset.

Executing the machining operation

Channel with start and end distances disabled

The channel is created 250mm from the selected cut and extends along the entire length of the piece, with a machining width of 100mm and a cut depth of 10mm.

Channel with start distance enabled and end distance disabled

The channel is created 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cut depth of 10mm.

As shown, with a start distance of 100mm, the channel starts 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with start distance disabled and end distance enabled

The channel is created 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cut depth of 10mm.

As shown, with an end distance of 100mm, the channel ends 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with start and end distances enabled

The channel is created 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cut depth of 10mm.

As shown, with a start distance of 100mm and an end distance of 100mm, the channel starts and ends 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with automatic drip grooves enabled

Drip grooves are automatically added to the piece (for drip grooves, see section 3.12.2).

The drip grooves are positioned halfway between the channel and the nearest cut.

Slab machining parameters

The operator can change the channel parameters from the slab machining parameters panel.

Machining with single passes

This screen shows the machining parameters for single passes.

Parameter description

Z position at work start
Sets the position at which the machine is maintained while it is not performing cuts.

Excess material
Thickness of material to be left above the required final section.

Arc step
Sets the arc discretisation step.

Check probing
Selects whether check probing is performed before the machining operation.

Machining with step passes

This screen shows the machining parameters for step passes.

Parameter description

Forward
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when the machine cuts in the direction of saw-blade rotation.

DOC3.13.15 FILLET

This function allows the operator to add a fillet to a vertex or side of the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

NOTE

The ‘Single vertex’, ‘Side’ and 'Polygon vertices’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the others.

Single vertex
Applies a single fillet to the selected vertex.

Side
Adds a fillet to the selected side.

Polygon vertices
Adds fillets to all vertices of the selected polygon.

Parameters for ‘Single vertex’ and ‘Polygon vertices’

Radius R
Fillet radius.

‘Side’ parameters

Offset 0
Specifies how much the piece is enlarged on the selected side, i.e. the side on which the fillet is applied.
The movement is inward if the value is negative and outward if it is positive.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

The application of fillets in the different modes is shown below. A preview of the machining operation allows the operator to see the expected result. The machining operation is actually applied only after it is confirmed using the green 'OK' button.

WARNING

!
Applying a fillet causes all settings previously applied to the piece cuts to be lost.

Executing a fillet on a single vertex

When this mode is selected, the machining operation can be performed on individual vertices of the piece.
To apply the machining operation correctly, the radius parameter cannot have a negative value.

In the following example image, three fillets with a radius of 100,0 mm have been applied.

The cut list on the left is affected as follows whenever a fillet is applied to a vertex:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • A curve, representing the new fillet, is inserted in the list.

  • The lengths of the sides adjacent to the selected vertex are reduced by the amount specified by the Radius parameter.

Executing a fillet on a side

When this mode is selected, the machining operation can be performed on the sides of the piece. In this mode, fillets have two main cases depending on the offset parameter value: a positive value and a negative value.

In the following example image, a fillet has been applied to the lower cut of the selected piece, with the offset parameter set to 100,0 mm.

The following image shows the opposite example: a fillet has been applied to the lower cut of the selected piece, with the offset parameter set to a negative value of -100mm.

The cut list on the left is affected as follows whenever a fillet is applied to a side:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • The selected straight cut is replaced by a curved cut.

    • With a positive offset value, the inserted fillet consists of a curve recessed relative to the selected polygon, whether internal or external.

    • Conversely, with a negative offset value, the applied fillet consists of a curve projecting outwards from the selected polygon.

Executing fillets on the vertices of the selected polygon

This mode applies one fillet to each vertex of the selected polygon.
For the machining operation to succeed, a negative radius value cannot be entered.
The following image shows the machining operation applied to all vertices of the piece:

As in Single Vertex mode, using this mode has the following effects on the cut list on the left:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • The selected straight cut is replaced by a curved cut.

    • With a positive offset value, the inserted fillet consists of a curve recessed relative to the selected polygon, whether internal or external.

    • Conversely, with a negative offset value, the applied fillet consists of a curve projecting outwards from the selected polygon.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.16 SPLIT

The ‘Split’ function divides the piece using a reference, a side, a perpendicular line or a custom line.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

To use this machining operation, first select one of the three available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

Parallel cut
In this mode, the dividing cut is performed along the longitudinal axis of the selected side.

Orthogonal cut
In this mode, the dividing cut is performed obliquely relative to the selected side, with its origin at the centre of the side.

Cut through two points
In this mode, the dividing cut is defined by manually specifying the coordinates of the two endpoints that determine the separation line between the pieces.

Parameters for ‘Parallel cut’ and ‘Orthogonal cut’

The following two controls can be enabled or disabled by clicking the check box to the right of ‘Cut extension’.

Cut extension

This function allows the operator to extend the cut applied to the selected side so that it covers the entire length of the piece in the cutting direction.

Offset

The operator can set the transverse distance of the cut, measured from the centre of the reference side.

Parameters for ‘Cut through two points’

The following control allows the coordinates of the two points forming the dividing line to be defined.

Set dividing-line point parameters

When the function is enabled, four parameter fields are available in which the operator can specify the coordinates (X, Y) of the start and end points of the cutting line.

Cut orientation
Using the dedicated command, the user can select a horizontal, vertical or free cut orientation relative to the previously set line start point.

Snap to vertices
When Free Cut is selected in the previous parameter, an additional parameter appears to its right. When enabled, it facilitates selection of the shape vertices when defining the cutting-line points.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Parallel cut

The following image shows a parallel cut performed on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Orthogonal cut

The following image shows an orthogonal cut performed on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Cut through two points

The following image shows a cut through two points performed using the vertex snapping function on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

The following image shows a cut through two points performed without using any special function on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Splitting pieces

When one or more pieces have been associated with the selected piece through Split operations, a dedicated button for managing associated pieces appears at the top of the “Edit Piece” panel.

Split pieces
Separates the split pieces from the original piece.

Before splitting, the associated pieces are managed as a single unit within the work area. In this state, they form a block of multiple elements that undergo the same operations and have not yet been separated.

For example, when one of the pieces generated using Split is added to the work area from the piece list, all other associated elements are also inserted automatically.

When the Split Pieces button is pressed, each piece generated using Split is disassociated from the original piece and treated as an independent item.

The associated-piece list previously shown above the preview in the Edit Piece panel and the Split Pieces button then disappear from the interface.

WARNING

!
The piece splitting operation cannot be undone once executed.

DOC3.13.17 INTERNAL CUT-OUT

The ‘Internal Cut-out’ function adds a rectangular, circular or elliptical internal cut-out to the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first select one of the two available modes by pressing the corresponding button:

NOTE

The ‘Rectangular’, 'Circular’ and 'Elliptical' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the others.

Rectangular cut-out
Selecting this mode provides access to the specific parameters required to perform a rectangular cut-out.

Circular cut-out
Selecting this mode provides access to the specific parameters required to perform a circular cut-out.

Elliptical cut-out
Selecting this mode provides access to the specific parameters required to perform an elliptical cut-out.

Rectangular Cut-out

When this mode is enabled, the rectangular cut-out preview is displayed directly in the machining preview and highlighted in light green. The size and position of the cut-out depend on the default parameters, which can be changed by the user.

Rectangular cut-out parameters

In this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the cut-out edge and the reference side of the selected piece.

Centre offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the centre of the cut-out.

NOTE

For curved cuts, a button can be used to select whether centre offset D is specified in mm or degrees.

Height H

Cut-out height.

Width W

Cut-out width.

Executing a rectangular cut-out

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Confirming the machining operation adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Circular Cut-out

When this mode is enabled, the circular cut-out preview is displayed directly in the machining preview and highlighted in light green. The size and position of the cut-out depend on the default parameters, which can be changed by the user.

Circular cut-out parameters

In this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the cut-out edge and the reference side of the selected piece.

Centre offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the centre of the cut-out.

NOTE

For curved cuts, a small button can be used to select whether centre offset D is specified in mm or degrees.

Radius R

Cut-out radius.

Executing a circular cut-out

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Confirming the machining operation adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Elliptical Cut-out

When this mode is enabled, the elliptical cut-out preview is displayed directly in the machining preview and highlighted in light green. The size and position of the cut-out depend on the default parameters, which can be changed by the user.

Elliptical cut-out parameters

In this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the cut-out edge and the reference side of the selected piece.

Centre offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the centre of the cut-out.

NOTE

For curved cuts, a button can be used to select whether centre offset D is specified in mm or degrees.

A

Value corresponding to the semi-major axis of the elliptical cut-out.

B

Value corresponding to the semi-minor axis of the elliptical cut-out.

Executing an elliptical cut-out

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Confirming the machining operation adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Optional tap holes

Pressing the button to the left of the OK button enables the tap-hole option. This option creates additional holes around the main central hole and displays additional parameters to configure.

NOTE

If the tap-hole diameter is equal to or less than the maximum hole radius, the tap holes are created as holes; if the tap-hole diameter is greater than the maximum hole radius, the tap holes are created as internal cut-outs.

Tap-hole parameters

In this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Number of holes

Specifies how many holes are applied to the current machining operation on the selected cut.

Hole diameter

Specifies the diameter of the holes applied to the machining operation.

Distance between holes

Specifies the distance measured between the centres of two consecutive holes.

Distance from cut-out

Specifies the distance between the hole centre and the cut-out edge.

Executing tap holes

NOTE
The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Confirming the machining operation adds a new internal polygon to the piece together with the tap holes, both graphically and in the added operations list on the left:

DOC3.13.18 DRAIN BOARD FLUTES

This function applies machining operations using the milling cutter currently mounted on the machine to the selected cut, whether curved or straight, in order to create drain board flutes.

Parameters

The result varies according to the values of the following parameters:

Number of flutes

Specifies how many flutes are applied to the current machining operation on the selected cut.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when flute insertion by number is selected.

Recalculate number
Recalculates the number of flutes so that they fill the selected cut.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when flute insertion by number is selected.

Length

Specifies how far the flutes extend into the cut.

Distance

This value represents the distance between the flutes, taking into account the diameter of the mounted tool.

Start distance

This value defines the distance between the vertices of the flutes inside the piece, controlling the empty space separating them.

Internal extension

Specifies how far the flutes extend beyond the reference cut.

Start depth

Penetration into the material at the start point of the drain board flute.

Final depth

Penetration into the material at the end point of the drain board flute.

Flute type on arcs

Three modes are available for flutes on curves, as described below.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when a curved cut is selected.

Cut width

For flutes inserted in saw blade mode, the cut width variable is available.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when saw blade mode is selected for inserting the flutes.

Drip system overlap

For flutes inserted in Fill mode, the percentage can be changed.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when Fill mode is selected for inserting the flutes.

Recalculate number

Pressing the button to the right of the number of flutes fills the selected cut with as many flutes as possible, according to the values of the other parameters.
The following example image shows the result of filling with flutes, in contrast to the first image at the start of the chapter.

Flute insertion mode

The following flute insertion options are available:

Insertion by number
The flutes are inserted according to the entered number.

NOTE

If this insertion mode is selected, Fill insertion cannot be used, and vice versa.

Fill insertion
The flutes are inserted according to the entered distance.

Saw blade mode
The saw blade is used to cut the flutes.

NOTE

If this mode is selected, milling cutter mode cannot be used, and vice versa.

Milling cutter mode
The milling cutter is used to cut the flutes.

Flute modes on arcs

When a curved polygon cut is selected, a new parameter is displayed and can have one of three values:

Radial
The flutes are arranged along the curve so that they point towards the centre of the arc.

Arc alignment
The flutes are arranged parallel along the curve and have the same length.

Tangent alignment
The flutes are arranged parallel along the curve. Their length varies so that all endpoints inside the piece lie on the same straight line, while preserving the extension of the endpoints outside the piece.

Mode 1: Radial

In this mode, the flutes share an origin point and are perpendicular to the corresponding tangent on the selected curved cut.

Mode 2: Arc alignment

In this mode, the flutes are parallel to one another and aligned along the arc for both spacing and internal extension.

Mode 3: Tangent alignment

In this mode, the flutes are parallel to one another and aligned along the arc for the internal extension, while being extended until they reach the tangent at the distance specified by the Length value.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the required cut.

Once the required result has been obtained and is shown and continuously updated in the machining preview, the operator can confirm the operation by pressing the green “OK” button immediately below the set parameters.
The flutes shown in the preview are then applied to the selected cut. Their colour changes to dark green, both in the preview and subsequently in the work area, indicating that they have been applied.

The cut list on the left is also updated according to the new machining operation and the flute parameters.
Multiple operations of this type can be applied to a single cut, provided that their parameters are not duplicated.

DOC3.14 NESTING

The Nesting function automatically arranges pieces within the slab perimeter in an optimised manner.

Using the function

To use this function, create a piece list and define the perimeter within which the pieces are to be placed.

Then press the button: the program automatically arranges the pieces within the slab perimeter.

NOTE

The pieces are placed on the slab taking into account subsequent use of the suction-cup material handling system to resolve collisions between pieces and the defects marked on the slab.

If the solution found is not satisfactory, press the button again to apply Nesting once more and find a different configuration.

WARNING!

The program removes all pieces currently in the work area before performing Nesting.

The Nesting function arranges pieces using different placement strategies. Each time the button is pressed, the program changes the arrangement, up to a maximum of 4 solutions (the fifth attempt repeats the first solution).
The program arranges the pieces in 4 different ways so that the user can compare them and select the best arrangement.

Examples

The following are examples of how the Nesting function can be used.

  • It can be used to arrange simple-shaped pieces more quickly.

  • This function finds the arrangement and combination of pieces that fills the largest possible slab area.

  • Nesting does not place any piece inside the slab's avoid areas.

  • It can work with slab perimeters of any shape.

  • If several perimeters are present, Nesting arranges pieces in each of them.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.14.1 AUTOMATIC NESTING (OPTIONAL)

Automatic Nesting is particularly useful when there are many pieces to process and the different combinations can no longer be managed easily by an operator.
Different solutions may be generated depending on the set parameters. They are displayed on the screen and the operator can select the preferred configuration.

Buttons

Add
Allows the operator to create a configuration.

Delete
Allows the operator to delete a configuration.

Edit
Allows the operator to edit a configuration.

Execute
Calculates all configurations and adds the results to the list on the right.

Editing a configuration

Automatic Nesting allows the parameters used to calculate piece placement in the work area to be customised for each configuration.
Depending on the type of pieces to be processed, some strategies may provide better performance.

Name

Name of the configuration shown in the list.

Slab distance

Distance that pieces must maintain from the slab edge when positioned.

No. of solutions to search

Number of solutions calculated by Nesting. The best of all calculated solutions is selected.

No. of movement attempts

Number of attempts made by moving the piece if it does not fit within the slab perimeter.

Movement value

Distance by which the piece is moved in an attempt to place it within the slab perimeter.

No. of attempts on the same slab

Number of attempts made to place the piece within the same perimeter if it does not fit.

Solution calculation timeout

Maximum time allowed for calculating each individual solution.

Use list order

Forces the program to attempt to position the pieces within the perimeter in the order in which they appear in the piece list.

Use custom order

Allows the order in which pieces are placed within the slab perimeter to be selected according to certain piece properties.
To enable a sorting criterion, select the corresponding check box.
The criteria are applied from top to bottom. This means that pieces are sorted according to the first criterion. If two or more pieces have the same value for the property linked to the first criterion, they are sorted according to the next criterion, and so on for every criterion in the list.
For each criterion, ascending or descending order can be selected.

Force piece before moving to the next

Selects whether the program attempts to position the piece in different locations within the slab perimeter or moves on to placing the next piece without further attempts.

Fixed starting point

Selects the point on the perimeter from which piece placement starts.

Fix rows-columns mode

Selects whether pieces are placed according to a row, column or random arrangement logic.

Piece rotation mode

Selects the logic used to rotate pieces during placement attempts within the slab perimeter.

Use largest inscribed rectangle

When enabled, pieces are placed inside the largest-area rectangle contained within the perimeter.
Otherwise, Nesting attempts to arrange the pieces over the entire available perimeter area.

Enable Deep Nesting

When disabled, pieces are placed on the slab to optimise use of the suction-cup material handling system for resolving collisions.
When enabled, more complex piece combinations can be searched, although their arrangement may conflict with use of the handling system.

Executing Nesting

Pressing the blue arrow next to an item in the list calculates the Nesting using that configuration.
A preview of the result is added to the section on the right. It shows the arrangement of the pieces within the perimeter and the percentage of slab area covered by the pieces.

If the piece arrangement is unsatisfactory, press the blue arrow again to recalculate the result.

After all Nesting configurations have been executed, the results are arranged with those that occupy the largest slab area shown first.

After selecting the preferred configuration, press the confirm button and the pieces are positioned on the slab according to the selected arrangement. The operator can still change their positions in the work area.

NOTE

The pieces are placed on the slab taking into account subsequent use of the suction-cup material handling system to resolve collisions between pieces and the defects marked on the slab.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.15 INTERACTING WITH PIECES IN THE WORK AREA

The operator can change the positioning of pieces on the worktable by interacting with them in the work area.

Functions

Multiple selection
Selects or deselects several pieces at the same time.

Select all
Selects or deselects all pieces in the work area at the same time.

Remove pieces
Removes the selected pieces from the work area.

Move pieces
Opens a panel used to move the selected pieces by specified distances.

Rotate pieces
Opens a panel used to rotate the selected pieces through specified angles.

Undo operation
Undoes the last operation performed.

Magnetise pieces
Function used to join two cuts together.

Miter cut
Opens a panel used to incline a cut on a piece in the work area.

Edit commercial piece
Opens a panel used to change the dimensions of a commercial piece.

Select pieces

To select a piece, press inside it. The background of an unselected piece is light blue and the background of a selected piece is red.

NOTE

Normally, only one piece can be selected at a time.

Multiple selection

Pressing the button enables multiple-selection mode. In this mode, several pieces can be selected at the same time. To deselect a piece, press inside an already selected perimeter.

Select all pieces

This button selects or deselects all pieces in the work area at the same time.

Remove pieces

Pressing the button removes the selected pieces from the work area and returns them to the piece list so that they are available later.

Move pieces

To move the selected piece, press and hold inside the perimeter and drag it in the work area.
Alternatively, use the directional-arrow movement panel.

NOTE

This function is applied to all selected pieces. Several pieces can therefore be moved at the same time.

Buttons

Directional arrows
Buttons used to move the piece in different directions.
The movement distance can be set using the text box on the left.

Movement along side axis
Performs movements parallel or orthogonal to the selected side of the piece.
If several pieces are selected at the same time, they all move consistently relative to the selected side.

Move pieces along the standard axes

Move the piece 1500 mm to the left.

Move pieces along the side axis

Move the piece 1500 mm to the left relative to the axis of the piece side.
The relevant button must be enabled to do this.

Rotate pieces

To rotate the selected pieces, press and hold outside the perimeter and drag them in the work area.
Alternatively, use the panel for rotation through specified angles.

NOTE

This function is applied to all selected pieces. Several pieces can therefore be rotated at the same time.

Buttons

Clockwise rotation
Rotates the piece clockwise by the angle entered in the text box below.

Anticlockwise rotation
Rotates the piece anticlockwise by the angle entered in the text box below.

90_ rotation
Rotates the piece 90_ clockwise.

Apply rotation

Rotate the piece 45 degrees clockwise.

Undo operation

This function undoes the last operation performed.
For example, if the operator deletes a piece by mistake, pressing this button restores the state before the piece was deleted.

NOTE

There is no displayed history of changes, but pressing the button repeatedly undoes several operations.

DOC3.15.1 MAGNETICALLY ALIGNING PIECES

This function aligns the sides of different pieces.

Dragging pieces in the work area

When a piece is moved close to another piece, the adjacent sides turn yellow, as shown in the image below:

When the piece is released, it attaches perfectly to the side of the other piece:

If the cuts are not parallel, the piece is rotated until it is parallel to the cut.

Aligning two cuts

The magnet function can be used to align two cuts.
To do this, first select the cut to be moved and then the cut to which the piece is to be magnetically aligned.
The first cut moves so that it is parallel to the second selected cut.
If the cuts are not parallel, the piece is rotated until it is parallel to the cut.


Alignment with stress-relief cuts

In this mode, the cuts of a piece can be aligned with the stress-relief cuts of a slab.

Alignment with laser references

The same procedure can be used to magnetically align cuts with line-laser or crosshair-laser references.
For the line laser, the selected side is aligned with the reference.

For the crosshair laser, the piece is moved so that the laser reference coincides with the nearest vertex of the selected cut.

DOC3.17 LOAD WORKING

Buttons

Sort by date

Other buttons

Slab Matching
Allows pieces to be positioned in an office installation of Parametrix using an image of the slab, and then realigns the perimeter and pieces with the actual position of the same slab on the machine worktable.

Load state

Loading a state

From the main page, open the panel used to load a state.
Then select the file relating to the job to be reproduced.

After confirmation, the pieces are created and inserted into the work area with all operations that were applied to them.

A previously programmed job can likewise be loaded with all the operations performed.

This function is used to reload a previously saved job onto the machine.

Import DXF (Optional)

This function loads the state of a job saved in a DXF file.

Importing trimming cuts from the DXF layout

A slab and its trimming cuts can now be imported into Parametrix by drawing the cuts in a dedicated layer of the DXF file.

The name of the layer dedicated to trimming cuts must be defined with a Donatoni technician. Once configured, it can no longer be changed.

Within this layer, each trimming cut must be represented by a line.

WARNING!

The following rules must be observed when creating the DXF file:
the slab perimeter must be present;
the slab perimeter must be rectangular;
the perimeter sides must be horizontal or vertical and must not be rotated;
each trimming line must be parallel to one side of the rectangle;
there must be no more than one trimming line for each side;
if several lines are drawn for the same side, Parametrix uses only the one closest to the edge.

To import the file, open the Import layout from DXF page in Parametrix and select the required file.

Available settings

On the file-selection screen, certain settings can be changed using the buttons below the preview on the right-hand side of the screen.

Automatic mode
If the selected DXF file does not contain the trimming-cut layer, Parametrix adds the cuts automatically according to the perimeter settings in the http://pannello.Se panel. If the layer is present, the trimming cuts defined in the DXF file take priority for
trimming.

Magnet mode
Parametrix moves the trimming cuts slightly so that they overlap the nearest cut, provided the distance between them is sufficiently small. This automatic correction can help optimise cut execution.

Magnet distance
Defines the maximum permitted distance between a trimming cut and a piece cut for them to be overlapped using magnet mode. Trimming-cut recognition is available both during standard import and during import with Slab Matching.

Examples

The images show a DXF file containing the slab perimeter, pieces and trimming cuts, together with the result obtained after import into Parametrix.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.17.1 SLAB MATCHING

This function allows the operator to load a cutting project prepared in the office and adapt it to the actual position and dimensions of the slab on the machine.

Buttons

X-axis offset
Movement of the perimeter along the X axis relative to its original position.

Y-axis offset
Movement of the perimeter along the Y axis relative to its original position.

Rotation
Difference in perimeter rotation relative to its initial position.

Directional movement arrows
Each button moves the perimeter in the direction indicated by the arrow.
The movement distance is specified in the text box below.

Clockwise/anticlockwise rotation
Rotates the perimeter anticlockwise and clockwise, respectively.
The rotation angle is specified in the text box below.

Reset positioning
Resets the perimeter to its initially imported position.

Automatic Slab Matching
Automatically aligns the perimeter.

Show/Hide pieces
Shows/hides the perimeters of the pieces in the work area.

Using Slab Matching

The operator can plan a slab cutting project in the office using a photo taken from the camera stand and save it.

After taking a photo of the slab on the worktable, the machine operator can load the project file saved in the office using the Slab Matching function.

The window that opens shows the photo taken of the worktable and a preview of the perimeter of the slab programmed in the office.

The elements visible on the screen represent:

Blue

Perimeter of the slab programmed in the office.

Fuchsia

Perimeters of the pieces within the slab programmed in the office.

Red

Original position of the slab programmed in the office.

Green

Position of the slab on the worktable.

The operator can move and/or rotate the perimeter to the correct position within the work area by dragging it, using the arrows or using the automatic alignment button.
Once the perimeter is positioned correctly, press Confirm. The pieces are then shown on the actual slab in the positions defined in the file.

DOC3.19 MACHINE ON CUT

Allows the position of the piece in the work area to be checked against its position on the machine. When “Machine on cut” is activated, a cut is selected on the screen and the machine moves to the corresponding position.
This operation is useful for checking whether a cut lies within the material.

 

 

Operation

Pressing the button displays the machine in the work area.

When one of the cuts is selected, the machine moves so that the centre of the saw blade is positioned on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

NOTE

Any type of cut can be selected, including core drilling and milling operations.

WARNING!

To perform the movement, the machine A axis must be at 0_

Advanced mode (Optional)

Advanced mode allows different machine elements to be positioned on the selected point.
When the function is activated, the following panel appears:

Saw blade centre alignment
Positions the centre of the saw blade on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

Crosshair laser alignment
Positions the crosshair laser on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

Second tool alignment
Positions the second tool (milling cutter or core drill) on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

Tool Plus alignment
Positions the Tool Plus on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

NOTE

The fourth and last button on the panel is visible only if the machine is equipped with the “Tool Plus”.

Saw blade centre alignment

This is equivalent to standard mode. The machine moves so that the centre of the saw blade is positioned on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

Crosshair laser alignment

The machine moves so that the crosshair laser pointer is positioned on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

Milling cutter or core drill alignment

The machine moves so that the centre of the second tool mounted on the machine, whether a milling cutter or core drill, is positioned on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

WARNING!

To use this function, move the A-axis inclination to 90_.

 

Tool Plus alignment

The machine moves so that the centre of the tool mounted on the Tool Plus is positioned on the endpoint of the cut closest to the selected point.

DOC3.21.1.1 EDIT CUT

This panel allows the operator to modify certain characteristics of a cut.

Buttons

In the top-left corner, the cut can be enabled or disabled.

Enable/Disable cut
Enables or disables the selected cut.

NOTE

A disabled cut is not performed by the machine.

Different versions of this panel are displayed according to the type of cut selected.

Saw blade cuts

When a linear or arc cut made with the saw blade is selected, the following panel is displayed:

Cuts made with the saw blade have a start point and an end point. The arrows define the travel direction, from start to end.

The table below shows the buttons that the operator can use to modify the cut characteristics:

Reverse cut direction
The operator can reverse the cut execution direction.

Extension amount
Changes the length of each cut extension.

Calculate overcut
Recalculates the cut extension according to the saw blade diameter and material thickness so that it matches the saw blade overcut.

Extend cut
Extends the cut by the specified extension amount.
The button on the left extends the start of the cut, while the button on the right extends the end.

Shorten cut
Shortens the cut by the specified extension amount.
The button on the left shortens the start of the cut, while the button on the right shortens the end.

Extend start point to slab edge
Extends the start of the cut to the edge of the slab.
The value in the box is used to extend the cut by a specified amount beyond the slab.

Extend end point to slab edge
Extends the end of the cut to the edge of the slab.
The value in the box is used to extend the cut by a specified amount beyond the slab.

Extend short cuts
If the selected cut is too short for the saw blade to penetrate the material completely, this button extends it, where possible, until it becomes a through cut.

Additional cut execution data is also displayed.

Plunge
Cut penetration into the material. The operator can modify this value.

Speed percentage
Percentage of the set speed used to perform the cut. The operator can modify this value.

NOTE

The speed percentage of arc cuts cannot be modified.

Inclination
Cut inclination in degrees. This value cannot be modified.

Edit the cut from the work area

Select a cut in the work area and press the right mouse button to open a window for quickly editing the cut.

The buttons correspond to the functions already listed. The end of the cut closest to the point where the button was pressed is extended.

Internal arc cuts

For arc cuts whose curvature faces towards the inside of the piece, the saw blade overcut may damage the side during machining and must therefore be taken into account.
For this reason, these cuts must be performed differently from external cuts.

Parametrix provides two modes for cutting internal arcs, selectable using the button in the top-right corner.

Tilted arc
A dimensioned miter cut is performed. The appropriate inclination is calculated automatically.

Offset arc
The cut is performed without inclination, but is shifted towards the outside of the piece from its correct position.

NOTE

By default, Parametrix recommends machining these cuts in “tilted arc“ mode.
If this mode is not required, the execution mode of each cut must be changed individually.

Each machining mode has advantages and disadvantages:

  • Tilted arcs provide a better finish on the final result, which therefore requires less manual finishing.
    However, they place greater stress on the machine, so machining must be performed at lower speeds and in more passes.

  • Offset arcs place less stress on the machine and can therefore be performed at higher speeds.
    However, the saw blade overcut causes greater damage to the material, and more material must be removed during manual finishing.

Holes and Milling Operations

Machining operations such as holes and milling allow fewer modifications by the operator.

Information is available for:

Plunge
Cut penetration into the material. The operator can modify this value.

Tool diameter
Displays the diameter of the tool used for the cut.

Recesses and Corner Holes

Corner holes and recesses are machining operations consisting respectively of multiple holes and milling operations. When one of these items is selected, a list of all its constituent cuts is displayed.

The operator can enable or disable each cut individually using the button on each list item, or act on all cuts in the machining operation simultaneously using the button at the top.
The buttons below the list change the order in which the individual cuts are performed.

Move using arrows
Moves the selected cut up or down in the list.

Move to the required position
Moves the selected cut to the position specified in the adjacent text box.

The operator can also modify the machining penetration using the field below:

Plunge
Penetration of the cuts into the material. The operator can modify this value.

NOTE

The plunge is the same for all cuts making up the machining operation.
Changing this value changes the penetration of all cuts in the list.

DOC3.21.4 MATERIAL HANDLING WITH SUCTION CUPS

This function divides the slab and moves the material using the suction cups.

Buttons

Manual movement
Gives the operator full control over the movements to be performed.

Automatic movement
Automatically performs the most suitable movements.

Manual movement

This function allows the operator to divide the slab using cuts and move the material to the required position using the suction cups.
Depending on the number of selected cuts, this function has two modes.

Single-selection mode

To perform a movement using the suction cups, select a saw blade cut, either linear or arc, and press the button.
The cut is extended to the slab edge where possible.
If the selected cut is inclined, a dedicated linear cut is added automatically so that the slab can be divided.

The following panel opens, where the direction, orientation and distance of the required movement can be specified.

The right-hand section contains these buttons:

Directional movement
Moves part of the cut slab in one of the directions.
The movement distance can be changed in the text box below.

Select an arrow in the work area or press one of the buttons on the right to select the direction and orientation of the movement.
The slab is divided and moved according to the type of cut selected.
In both cases, the slab movement distance can be changed in the text box below the four directional buttons.

The selected cut is moved as high as possible in the list of cuts to be performed. The suction-cup movement is executed immediately afterwards.

WARNING!

The operator is responsible for checking whether the movement is feasible.

Multiple-selection mode

Multiple-selection mode allows pieces of any shape to be lifted. To do this, select the cuts required to divide the slab using multiple-selection mode.

After making the selection, press the button to start the procedure.

The selected cuts are extended, where possible, to form a continuous path that divides the slab. If one or more selected cuts are inclined, they are automatically replaced with non-inclined cuts.

The following panel then opens.

After selecting the slab section to be moved, the movement can be defined by dragging it in the work area or using one of the following buttons:

Step
Enter the movement distance in mm applied whenever one of the directional buttons is pressed.

Movement along the axes
These boxes display values representing the vertical and horizontal movement of the slab relative to its starting position.
The values can be changed manually to define the slab movement.

Cut collision check
Parametrix automatically checks that no protruding cut damages the other section of material at the new slab position. If a problem is detected, the slab is moved to the nearest suitable position.
This check can be disabled to give the operator full control over the movement.

Restore original position
Returns the moved slab section to its original position.

When confirmed, the selected cuts are moved to the top of the list of cuts to be performed. The suction-cup movement is executed immediately afterwards.

WARNING!

Multiple-selection mode allows pieces of any shape, including overhanging pieces, to be lifted.
The operator is responsible for checking whether the movement is feasible.

Rules for a valid cut selection

To divide the slab correctly, the following cut-selection instructions must be observed.

  • The selected cuts may be saw blade cuts, either straight lines or arcs, milling operations, or multiple holes at corners.

  • The selected cuts must form a path that divides the slab into two sections. Cuts forming a closed path cannot be selected.

  • The program automatically extends linear saw blade cuts until a solution that divides the slab is found. Arc cuts, milling operations and holes are not modified automatically.
    It is therefore advisable for the first and last cuts in the path to be linear saw blade cuts.

  • At internal corners where saw blade overcut does not separate the material completely, vertex milling operations or multiple holes must be inserted.

  • The penetration of the selected cuts must be sufficient to separate the slab.

  • The first and last cuts must be able to extend outside the slab.

Operation not possible message

If the program considers the movement operation impossible, the causes may be as follows:

  • The selected cuts are insufficient to create a path that divides the slab into two sections;

  • The selected cuts form a closed path;

  • The selected cuts cannot detach the piece because of saw blade overcut;

  • Extending the selected cuts would damage other pieces;

  • The penetration of at least one selected cut is insufficient to separate the slab;

Automatic movement

This function attempts to resolve automatically situations in which one or more pieces in the work area would be damaged by other cuts.

The algorithm analyses the cut arrangement and independently determines how and where to perform movements, optimising the operation sequence.

However, automatic calculation cannot always manage every situation. In particularly complex cases, manual intervention may be required to complete or correct the movements.

WARNING!

The operator is responsible for checking whether the movements are feasible.

Changing the suction cup position

During this phase, the operator can change both the suction cup gripping position and activation of the corresponding vacuum zones to ensure an optimal and safe grip on the material.
To do this, select the “Move“ item in the list and press the cut editing button.

The buttons in this panel allow the operator to interact with the suction cups.

Directional movement
Changes the suction cup position.
The distance of this movement can be selected in the text box below.

NOTE

The suction cups can also be moved by interacting with them in the work area.

Suction cup rotation
Rotates the suction cups about their axis.
The value in the adjacent text box indicates how far the suction cup assembly rotates each time an arrow is clicked.

Suction cup assembly diagram
The suction cup assembly diagram allows the operator to select which vacuum zones are switched on or off during movement. If a zone is green, the machine activates the vacuum; if it is red, it does not.
The example on the left shows zones 5 and 6 switched off.

Reverse operation order (Optional)

This optional function can be enabled to reverse the order of the operations.

For example, if the following operations are selected:

  • First bottom cuts

  • External internal

  • First left cuts

The actual order of the operations is:

  • External internal

  • First bottom cuts

This occurs because the positions are overwritten. This optional function is provided so that the operation order can follow the chronological selection order.

With this function enabled, the operation order in this case is:

  • First bottom cuts

  • External internal

  • First left cuts

Activating a macro

Once the macro has been created and modified as required, it can be selected and activated.

Enable macro disabled
Each unselected macro has a disabled macro activation button immediately to its right.

Enable macro enabled
The macro currently selected but not yet activated has the same button as the others, but it is green to indicate that it can be enabled.

Macro activated
The currently loaded macro is highlighted in green and has a symbol immediately to its right confirming that it has been loaded.
The name of the loaded macro is also displayed in the parameter User Values, under “Active operation”:

Procedure for creating and loading a macro

The first step is to ensure that the activation button is set to ON, so that the required macro can subsequently be used.

Create a new operation and assign it a name. Then click the new operation, now visible in the list, and immediately afterwards click the edit button on the right-hand side of the panel to open the macro editing panel.
For each operation type, select the required operations from the list on the left (Available) and add them to the list of selected operations. The configuration can then be confirmed so that it can be displayed and managed in the operations panel.
The macro can be loaded by clicking the button immediately to the right of the macro name.
The following is an example of the macro named “operazione_1“, containing 3 operations shown on the right and highlighted in green with the corresponding symbol because it is in the “loaded“ state.

The first step is to ensure that the activation button is set to ON, as this is required to use the selected macro. Once enabled, create a new operation and assign it an identifying name. After creation, the operation appears in the list: select it and click the edit button on the right-hand side of the panel to open the macro configuration interface.

In this interface, for each operation type, the required items can be selected from the list on the left (labelled "Available") and added to the list on the right, which contains the selected operations. Once the selection is complete, confirm the configuration to make it visible and manageable in the operations panel.

The macro can be loaded by clicking the dedicated button immediately to the right of the assigned macro name. For example, consider the macro named “operazione_1”: it contains three operations, displayed in the panel on the right, and is highlighted in green with the corresponding symbol indicating that it is in the “loaded” state.

DOC3.21.8 ISO CONTROL PAGE

This screen provides real-time monitoring of the ISO program being executed by the machine.

Job name and elapsed time

This section displays information about the machine motors.

Motor

Main spindle motor.

External motor

Tool Plus motor, if present.

The information page can be changed using the buttons below.

Previous/Next information panel
These buttons allow the operator to change the category of displayed information.

The following is shown for each motor:

Consumption

Indicates the current drawn by the motor.

Alarm threshold

Indicates the current threshold in amperes above which the alarm is activated and motor rotation is stopped.
Set the value according to the mounted tool and the machining operation being performed.

RPM

Indicates the motor speed in revolutions per minute.
The value is positive for clockwise rotation and negative for anticlockwise rotation.

Axes

This section displays information about the machine axes.

Actual

Displays the current coordinates for the position and orientation of the machine axes.

Distance to go

Displays the distance of each axis from the coordinates at which the cut ends.

Consumption

Manual controls

If problems occur while the job is being executed, certain machine functions can be controlled using manual commands.

Manual controls
Opens the manual control window for managing water and suction cups.

Water

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the tool.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

Suction cups

Enable/disable suction cups
The screen shows a top view of the suction cup assembly divided into its different zones. Pressing a zone changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is configured to generate a vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is configured for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Park suction cups
Pressing the button retracts the suction cups to their rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
Pressing the button lowers the suction cups from the parking position to the limit stop. Make sure there is enough space for the suction cups to extend fully.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
Pressing the button lowers the Z axis until the material contacts the work surface, switches off the vacuum pump and activates blowing from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
This control brings the suction cups into contact with the material, activates the vacuum pump in the areas marked green and blowing in the areas marked red. When the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blowing control
The button switches blowing on or off from the suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

This function provides a rendering of the project and shows in real time the pattern that will appear on the pieces, allowing them to be positioned on the slabs so that the stone patterns match.

Buttons

Book Match
Allows slabs to be programmed in Book Match mode.

Design modes

Book Match patterns can be programmed in two different modes.

Easy Match

Designed for sequential processing.
It allows one slab to be managed at a time, and the overall view is available only after all required slabs have been processed.
Recommended for on-machine programming.

Project Match

Designed for large projects.

DOC3.22.1 EASY MATCH (OPTIONAL)

The Easy Match function shows in real time the pattern that the pieces will have in the original positions in which they were designed, while they are moved over a slab on the worktable.

NOTE

Easy Match mode works only with pieces imported from DXF files.

Buttons

After pressing the button, the following panel opens:

Side-by-side view
Displays both the project preview and the worktable on the same screen.

Preview view
Allows pieces to be moved by clicking inside their perimeter, enabling more precise positioning.

Worktable view
Allows pieces to be moved on the worktable using the full screen.

Saves an image representing the preview of the current project.

Opens a screen for changing the arrangement of items in the project preview.

Preview view

Allows pieces to be moved by clicking inside their perimeter, enabling more precise positioning.

The preview displays all pieces from the imported file in the exact positions in which they were designed.
The preview size corresponds at a 1:1 scale to the size of the designed pieces.
Pieces added to the worktable take on the slab colour, while those not yet added have a uniform background.

From the preview, it is possible to:

  • Add a piece to the work area by clicking inside the area to be machined.

  • Move a piece located on the worktable.

  • Select a piece on the worktable by clicking inside the piece.

  • Delete a piece from the preview by selecting the eraser below the piece list and then selecting the piece to be deleted in the preview. The piece is also deleted from the worktable and the piece list.

Worktable view

Classic Parametrix worktable view. It allows pieces to be moved on the worktable using the full screen.

Side-by-side view

Displays both the project preview and the worktable on the same screen.

Saving the preview

Saves the preview of the current job.
The following screen opens:

The operator is asked to choose the preview name, whether to save it as an image or PDF, where to save it and its resolution.
The resolution options are Auto (automatic resolution), Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Custom (the operator selects the exact resolution).
Once confirmed, the preview image or PDF opens automatically.

Editing the preview

On this screen, the pieces in the preview can be arranged as required.
All changes made are also displayed later in the other views.

The top bar contains the following buttons.

Move pieces
Moves the pieces in the preview.
The buttons in the bottom bar of the window are displayed.

Pan view
Moves the preview view with all pieces.

In the program parameters panel, on the User Values tab, the colours of certain project-preview elements can be changed.

Perimeter

Shows/hides the piece perimeters in the preview.
The display colour can be changed using the adjacent button.

Name

Shows/hides the piece names in the preview.
The display colour can be changed using the adjacent button.

Background

Sets the preview background colour.

Remove background
Removes the background from the preview.

Workflow

To work using Easy Match, import the project into Parametrix from a DXF file.
The program displays a Book Match preview for the pieces in the file.

After taking a photo of the worktable, the pieces to be cut can be placed on the slab.
This can be done using the standard procedure from the piece list or by pressing inside the perimeter of one of the pieces shown in the preview.

Dragging a piece in the preview also moves it on the slab, which is useful for matching the veining between pieces.
The reverse is also possible: drag the piece on the slab and use the preview to check whether the veining matches at the new position.

At this point, follow the standard machining procedure: create the ISO program and cut the slab.
When completed, press the button to proceed to the next job.
The project progress is retained in the preview.
Acquire the photo of a new slab and place the pieces inside its perimeter.

Continue in this way until the project is completed.

Project planning

Create a new project

The operator creates a new project by specifying its name, the number of rows and columns it contains, bearing in mind that each cell corresponds to a slab, and the cell dimensions. Once confirmed, the following screen is displayed:

Add the slabs

At this point, import the pieces to be cut. Both DXF files and standard pieces can be loaded. There is no limit to the number of files that can be loaded.

They will then be inserted onto the slab in the selected work area.

DOC3.23 UNLOAD PIECE (OPTIONAL)

This function can be used to program the movement of a piece to a predefined machine position.
The program calculates the movement of the centre of the piece to machine X, Y and Z coordinates defined in the parameters. 

Methods for adding an Unload Piece operation

Single
Applies one operation to a selected piece.

All pieces
Applies the piece unloading operation to every piece placed in the work area.

Single

After Single mode has been activated, click the piece to be unloaded.
The following example image shows the function applied to the piece positioned in the centre, with the corresponding cut added to the cut list on the right:

All pieces

This mode automatically unloads all pieces in the work area. The corresponding cuts are therefore added to the list displayed in the right-hand side panel.
The following is an example after the mode has been executed:

Required precautions

The program does not perform checks to prevent material movement in certain special situations that may occur.
These checks are the responsibility of the machine operator.

Particular attention must be paid to the following situations:

  • Miter cuts: if the piece has miter cuts, it may remain trapped in the slab.

  • Piece with cuts flush with the saw blade: the piece may not be cut completely. In this case, when the function attempts to lift the piece, it will remain attached to the slab.

  • Cuts inside the perimeter: if there are cuts inside the piece perimeter, check and, if necessary, move the suction cup positions to obtain a vacuum.

DOC3.26 CUT SIMULATION

This function displays a simulation of the operations performed on the piece.

 

 

Buttons

The bottom bar of the Parametrix cut editing screen contains the button used to open the cut simulation function.

Cut simulation
This button opens and closes the cut simulation screen.

 

Managing the cut simulation

The simulation is controlled using these buttons:

Start
This button starts the simulation.

Pause
This button temporarily pauses the simulation.

Restart
This button restarts the simulation from the beginning.

Simulation speed
This button adjusts the simulation speed by selecting one of the three available levels.

 

Cut simulation

The simulation starts with the machine in the parking position. The milling cutter or saw blade then performs the cuts in the sequence defined in the queue displayed in the right-hand column. At the end of each step, the completed item is highlighted in green.

Different actions or events can be added to the simulation queue and their order can be changed, allowing the sequence to be adapted to the specific job requirements and making the simulation more effective for its intended purpose.

DOC4 PARAMETRIX SX

Parametrix includes a version designed specifically to simplify the workflow on SX-category machines.
In particular, it allows the operator to manage combinations of cuts efficiently in order to optimise the production process.
This chapter describes the functions that differ from the standard version of Parametrix.

Side section

The buttons at the top right allow the operator to change the Parametrix screen.

Each screen is dedicated to a specific aspect of slab machining.

Piece positioning
Parametrix main screen.
The following operations are performed:

  • creating and editing pieces;

  • acquiring the photograph of the slab on the worktable and its perimeter;

  • positioning pieces in the work area;

Cut optimisation and management
Screen for optimising and managing cuts.
The following operations are managed:

  • moving material with suction cups;

  • washing the worktable;

  • editing cuts to optimise their combinations;

Cut combination
Final workflow screen.
The following operations are managed:

  • displaying and sorting cut combinations;

  • managing the unloader;

  • starting the machine cutting program;
