DOC4.1 MANUAL CONTROLS PAGE

When the application starts, if the axes have already been homed, the following home screen is displayed:

WARNING!

When starting the machine, exercise extreme caution if moving the axes before the homing procedure has been performed. Collisions with the machine's mechanical limit stops could occur and compromise correct operation.

Top bar

Parameters
Provides access to the Parametrix program parameters.

Tool Parameters
Pressing the button opens the tool parameters page. See the “Tool Configuration” chapter for a detailed description of the parameters page.

Automatic 0/90-degree rotation
The “C” axis automatically moves to 0 or 90 degrees when the button is pressed.

Automatic parking
When the button is pressed, the machine automatically moves the “X”, “Y”, “Z” and “C” axes to the zero position.
The machine performs the movements in the following order:
(A) - “Z” axis to the absolute zero position;
(B) - “C” axis to the absolute 0 position;
(C) - “X” and “Y” axes simultaneously to the absolute zero position;

WARNING!

Certain safety conditions must be met before automatic parking can be performed:
The “A” axis must be at 0_.
Make sure that the movement area involved in positioning (see adjacent figure) is clear.

Zero
Homes the axes (this operation is required when the machine is started or when the rectangular indicators are red).
When the homing cycle is complete, the indicators turn grey.
The homing procedure moves the axes in the following sequence:

  1. Z axis

  2. A axis

  3. C axis

  4. X and Y axes simultaneously

  5. B axis (Optional: controlled lathe)

NOTE

Homing is permitted only when the coded key is inserted in the appropriate station on the operator console.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the tool.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes colour: Green = On; Red = Off.

Manual Tool Change
Pressing the button starts the tool-change procedure.

Maintenance
Pressing this button displays a window containing all machine maintenance operations.
Both maintenance operations that are due and those that are within the normal interval are displayed.
If at least one maintenance operation requires.

Help
Pressing this button slightly changes the appearance and behaviour of all buttons currently displayed. Any button with a small question mark in the top-left corner can then be pressed to display a short message explaining its function. To exit this help mode, simply press the “Help” button again.

Right-hand sidebar

When the application starts, MANUAL is the preselected function.
This sidebar contains the following available controls and programs/functions:

Central area

The central area consists of the following elements, described in detail below:

  • Axes

  • Controls

  • Saw blade management

  • Feed

  • Suction cups

Axes

This interface displays the values of the machine axes.

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes already homed:

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes not yet homed:

The elements in this common interface section are explained below, using the already-homed axes configuration as a reference.

Actual position: indicates the position of the axis relative to the active origin.
Target position: indicates the position to be set in order to move the axis by pressing the MDI or RTCP button.
F: Feed, movement speed expressed in mm/min.
DTG: Distance To Go, distance from the target.
A: Amperes.

Reset Axis
Pressing this button sets the zero point of the active origin at the current position of the corresponding axis (X, Y or Z).
The axis reset operation can only be performed for origins other than 0 (zero).
To use the tool-coordinate origin (TCP), the correct dimensions of the mounted tool must be set before pressing the Reset Axis button.

Automatic _90-degree rotation
The position of the “C” axis is increased by 90 degrees clockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 12 degrees, pressing the “Automatic _90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 102 degrees: 12 _ 90.

Automatic -90-degree rotation
The position of the “C” axis is decreased by 90 degrees anticlockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 102 degrees, pressing the “Automatic -90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 12 degrees: 102 - 90.

Controls

This panel contains several buttons whose behaviour is explained below:

MAN (Enable manual movement)
To operate the machine manually, the spindles must be positioned correctly and certain functions must be enabled. This button is provided for that purpose.

NOTE

When manual operation is enabled, the adjacent indicator LED turns green.

Suction-cup axis
Reference axis on which the suction cups are mounted.

Alarm threshold
Indicates the threshold above which the alarm is activated and spindle rotation is stopped.

Selected origin
Clicking the “Origin” field allows the operator to change the origin used for machining.
Changing this field updates the Axes values.
Origin values can range from 0 to 19 inclusive.

MDI
When pressed, the machine moves until it reaches the values set as the target positions (see above).
The speed of the X and Y axes is controlled by their respective potentiometers, while the other axes are controlled by the interpolated potentiometer.

Saw blade management

Only one of the windows available to the operator for managing the installed saw blades is shown below, as the remaining windows provide similar functions.

First reference axis
First reference axis for each saw blade (X1 for DISK1 in the example)

NOTE

When positioning the X axes, the centre of the saw blade is used as the reference for the target
position; the current position differs by half the blade core thickness.

Second reference axis
Second reference axis for each saw blade (Z1 for DISK1 in the example)

Start/Stop spindle rotation
Controls switching the saw blade on and off for the corresponding spindle.
The saw blade speed is selected in the tool parameters.

Enable/Disable external spindle water
Controls switching the water supply for the selected tool on and off.

Current consumption
Indicates the current drawn by the spindle motor.

Feed

The Feed value represents the machine's interpolated movement.

Suction cups

The suction cups can be operated manually to move pieces from one work area to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable/disable suction cups
The screen shows a top view of the suction cup assembly divided into its different zones. Pressing a zone changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is configured to generate a vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is configured for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Park suction cups
Pressing the button retracts the suction cups to their rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
Pressing the button lowers the suction cups from the parking position to the limit stop. Make sure there is enough space for the suction cups to extend fully.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
Pressing the button lowers the Z axis until the material contacts the work surface, switches off the vacuum pump and activates blowing from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
This control brings the suction cups into contact with the material, activates the vacuum pump in the areas marked green and blowing in the areas marked red. When the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

BLOW - Blowing control
The button switches blowing on or off from the suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, making sure that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that the material has no defects or breaks that could create hazards or cause machine malfunctions.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom button has no effect on the vacuum pump, which continues to operate. The pump can be forced off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, a dedicated sensor checks the vacuum status. If an adequate vacuum level is not detected, the “vacuum failure” alarm appears. The pump remains active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes the vacuum to drop rapidly, resulting in the material lifted by the suction cups falling.

Bottom bar

The bottom bar displays information and error messages, together with buttons for certain functions.
Three examples of the bottom bar are shown below:

  • No active alarms.

  • With a general emergency enabled, indicated by an icon, an error code (PE0000 in this example), its description and the flashing alarms button on the right.

  • With a displayed message; in this example, direct JOG is active.

Alarms
Allows the operator to open the alarms window.

Minimise software
Allows the operator to leave the software page.

Machine shutdown
Allows the operator to shut down the machine completely.

Alarms

The alarms page shows the system's active Alarms/Messages.
If the machine has no active alarms, the page is empty; otherwise, one row is displayed for each active error.
The following example alarm management and display page shows an alarm that is active in the system:

Alarm buttons

Refresh
Updates the status of the machine alarms.

Alarm history
Displays the daily alarm history.

Messages / Alarms
Selects whether alarms or messages are displayed.

Alarm groups
Displays complete information about the alarms currently present on the machine.

Alarm display - Standard

The standard display for an alarm consists of:

Online link
A button containing a link to the relevant online guide.

Alarm code
Identification code for the problem that caused the alarm.

Description
A brief description of the detected error.

Alarm display - History

In addition to the elements already described, the daily alarm history includes the following data:

Status change time
Date and time at which the alarm status changed.

Alarm status
Status reached by the alarm (ON / OFF).

Alarm display - Groups

The grouping system displays a single entry for each alarm, avoiding duplicates.

Number of occurrences
The number of times the alarm has been activated.

First activation time
Date and time of the first alarm activation.

Last activation time
Date and time of the most recent alarm activation.

DOC4.1.1 ISO PROGRAM LIST

The ISO Program List page allows multiple programs, previously created using CAD-CAM software, to be run consecutively on machines with two work areas, Twin machines, or when multiple jobs are created while the machine is already running.

Top bar

The top bar displays information for monitoring the progress of the list.

List execution status
Indicates whether the list is currently running.

List progress bar
Shows the progress and execution status of the list.

List progress bar

This progress bar provides information on the execution status of the current ISO program, while also giving an overview of the next program in the list and the program that has already completed machining and moved to unloading.

In the previous image, no program is yet shown in the unloading phase because list execution has not started and no piece has been processed. Conversely, if the list contains only one ISO file, or if machining has started and all the other files have already been executed, the ‘Next’ section is empty.

During execution, program progress is displayed in real time, as shown below.

Side menu

The right side of the suction cup panel contains buttons for managing individual files in the program list.

Run next program
Moves the current program to unloading and loads the next program.

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upwards in the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down
Moves the selected ISO file downwards in the list of files to be executed.

Delete selected item
Removes the currently selected item from the list.
If multiple items are selected, only the first selected item is deleted.

Suction cup panel
Opens the panel for managing the suction cup zones.

Conveyor panel
Opens the conveyor management panel.

Suction Cup Panel

The suction cups can be operated manually to move pieces from one work area to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable/disable suction cups

Green indicates that the zone is configured to generate a vacuum.

Conveyor Panel

This page is used to manage slab loading and unloading via the conveyor belt located beneath the machine.

WARNING!

Before operating the conveyor controls, check the work area at both the line inlet and outlet for people, in order to avoid unnecessary risks.

Top bar buttons

Automatic slab loading
Starts the loading cycle, which follows this sequence:

  1. Move the loading roller conveyor until the slab contacts conveyor belt #1

  2. Move the conveyor belts until the slab reaches the preset inlet position. The slab position is referenced to the inlet edge.

Unload pieces
Starts the conveyor belts to move the material out of the work area. The travel distance is set in the software parameters.

Conveyor parameters

The page contains check boxes for selecting machine-specific options.

Move conveyor at end of program

Enables automatic movement of the machined pieces to the unloading area at the end of the executed program.

Enable robot

Enables the robot.

Wait for photo

Stops execution of the program list after each program.

Wash inside

Enables internal washing.

Wash below

Enables washing of the upper surface of the slab.

Wash above

Enables slab washing.

Bottom bar buttons

The dedicated buttons can be used to move the conveyor both to the right and to the left.

Manual conveyor movement to the left
The conveyor moves to the left.

Manual conveyor movement to the right
The conveyor moves to the right.

Bottom bar

The lower part of the bar displays functions relating to execution of the ISO program list, together with tool and slab monitoring information.

List execution management

The lower section also contains the two buttons for selecting program execution modes:

Manual / automatic
Defines whether the machine status is manual or automatic.

Single / automatic next
Defines whether the next program starts automatically.

Slab monitoring and probing cycles

In the centre and on the right of the bottom bar, the operator can configure periodic tool diameter monitoring by setting checks at intervals based on the number of cycles performed.

Number of cycles between saw blade probing operations
Sets the number of programs to be executed before probing is performed to measure the saw blade diameters.

Number of Cycles Until Next Probe
Indicates the number of cycles remaining before the next saw blade probing operation.

Slab thickness
Displays the slab thickness.

ISO Program List Execution

The ISO program list is expanded automatically as ISO programs are generated in Parametrix. The operator can nevertheless reposition items within the list or remove them as required.

Before executing the list, the operator can set the number of cycles to be performed between tool probing operations.
The number of cycles remaining until the next probing operation is then updated and displayed.

The operator starts execution of the program list by pressing the “Start cycle“ button. The programs are then executed in sequence, simultaneously displaying the current program, the program to be executed next and the program already completed.

If the program execution mode is set to Manual and Single, list execution stops at the end of the current program, immediately after preparing the next program for execution.
In this case, the operator can press the Next button when appropriate and continue execution by pressing the 'Start Cycle' button again.

DOC4.2 TOOL PANEL

This panel allows the operator to manage the machine's saw blades.

Parameters

The parameters of the selected saw-blade set are shown in this section.
The general parameters of the saw-blade set are shown on the left, while the parameters specific to the blade associated with each spindle unit are shown on the right.
For SX5 or SX6 machines, 5 or 6 saw blades respectively are shown in the right-hand section.

General saw-blade set parameters

The parameters in the left-hand section, relating to the selected saw-blade set, are listed below.

Name
Name of the saw-blade set.

Radius
Radius of the saw blades in the set.

NOTE

All saw blades in the set must have the same diameter.

Blade thickness
Average thickness of the saw blades in the set.

RPM
Revolutions per minute of the motors on which the saw blades are mounted.

Clearance position
Clearance position for the saw-blade set.

The following buttons are also available:

Recalculate thickness
Recalculates the average thickness of the saw blades.

RPM information
Opens a table containing recommended RPM values for machine operation.

Individual saw-blade parameters

Each of these elements displays the parameters of the saw blade mounted on the corresponding spindle unit.

The radius and thickness can be set for each saw blade. The operator can enable or disable the saw blade using the adjacent button.

Enable/Disable saw blade
Specifies whether or not to use the saw blade mounted on the corresponding spindle unit.

Buttons

Probe saw blade
Starts a saw-blade probing cycle.

Compensation
Opens the manual compensation window.

Complete data
Opens the window for editing saw-blade data.

Complete data

In this window, the operator can edit all data relating to the saw-blade set mounted on the machine.
In particular, the radius, tooth thickness and core thickness of each saw blade can be set.

In particular:

Blade thickness
Measurement of the saw-blade tooth thickness.

Core thickness
Measurement of the saw-blade core thickness.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.2.1 COMPENSATIONS

This function allows manual compensation to be applied to the distance between the machine stops.
Use it when a discrepancy is observed between the dimensions of the programmed pieces and the dimensions measured on the resulting pieces.

Required values

During the compensation procedure, the operator is asked to enter the following values.

Desired piece dimensions

Programmed dimension of the side of the pieces to be checked.

Piece

Measured dimension of the side of the piece whose ends were cut using the specified saw blade and the next one.

Thickness

Thickness of the saw blade mounted on the specified stop.

Finally, press the button.

Compensation
Applies the appropriate compensation.

Procedure

First, import two rectangular pieces of the same size into Parametrix.
Place them side by side on a slab as shown in the figure, then execute the job.

Open the window for manual stop compensation and complete the required fields.
Enter the original dimension of the side of the programmed rectangles.
Then enter the measured dimension of the same side of each cut rectangle, taking care to specify which saw blades were used.
Finally, enter the thickness of each saw blade mounted on the machine.

When finished, press the button below so that Parametrix calculates the compensation to be applied to each stop.

NOTE

Depending on the number of machine stops, more rectangles of suitable size for the worktable must be cut.

DOC4.3 CUT OPTIMISATION AND MANAGEMENT

The cut optimisation and management screen is opened using the second button at the top right.

Cut list

The cuts to be performed by the machine are shown in this list.

Using the cut list, the operator can:

  • Change the cut execution order.

  • Edit the characteristics of a cut.

  • Insert pauses between cuts.

List items

Enable/Disable cut
Indicates whether the cut is enabled or disabled for machining.
Pressing the button changes its status.

Cut type
Indicates the cut type (“Perimeter”, “Internal cut”, “Milling”, etc.).

Functions

The arrangement of the cuts in the list on the right indicates the order in which they are performed.
The buttons below can be used to change this order or insert a pause between one cut and the next.

Edit cut
Edits certain properties of the selected cut.

Insert pause
A pause can be inserted between the selected cut and the next cut.
The program performs all cuts before the pause, then stops the machine and waits for the operator to issue the Start command.
This can be used, for example, to change the tool.

Delete cut
When this function is enabled, an eraser icon appears next to each entry in the cut list.
Pressing the icon permanently removes the corresponding cut from the list.

Cut optimisation
Used to improve the combination of machine spindles during cutting.
Select the mode in the adjacent text box and press the button to apply the optimisations.

Additional piece properties
Edits the additional properties of the piece selected in the work area.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.3.1 CUT OPTIMISATION

The cut management page can apply SX machine optimisations to improve the combination of spindles during cutting.

Mode 1

This mode joins two different cuts lying on the same straight line to create a single cut.

Mode 2

Attempts to make all cuts the same (maximum) length.

Mode 3

Normally, after the movement system has been used, a cut cannot be manually moved to a position before the movement.
With this optimisation mode, the software places the cuts that the machine can perform before the movement.

Mode 4

Cuts of similar length are changed to the same length.

Mode 5

Extends all cuts beyond the slab edge and makes them similar in length, as in mode 2.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.4 CUT COMBINATION

This screen shows the spindle combinations used by the machine to perform the cuts.

Combined cut list

Each element in the list in the right-hand section shows the combination of spindles used to perform a set of cuts simultaneously.

NOTE

If a spindle is manually disabled using the dedicated control on the tool panel, it is not included in the cut combinations.

As with standard cuts, their order in the list can be changed and they can be disabled.

Enable/Disable cut
Indicates whether the cut is enabled or disabled for machining.
Pressing the button changes its status.

Move using arrows
Moves the selected cut up or down in the list.

Move to desired position
Moves the currently selected cut to the position specified in the adjacent text box.

Pause
Inserts a pause after the selected cut.

NOTE

Any operation performed on a list element affects all the cuts it contains.

Buttons

The following button is located on the bottom bar:

Display unloading
Opens a screen that allows the operator to create an unloading program for positioning rows of pieces on the dedicated conveyor belts.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.4.1 UNLOADER

The strip unloader is managed by the software, which creates an unloading program to position rows of pieces on the dedicated conveyor belts and verify the gripping positions and zones used.

Executing the machining operation

The software checks that the slab is divided into horizontal rows (allowing a tolerance of a few degrees in the cut direction), that the piece dimensions are within the limits, and sets the movement order and the row of suction cups to be used.
Suction cup movements to the right or left, intersecting pieces and other similar conditions prevent creation of the program, which will not be unloaded automatically.

The gripping zones are shown in green, while zones not used for gripping are shown in red.
The parameters are set by the technician during machine commissioning and remain fixed.
